probability-rules.summary: Elementar hodisalar fazosi, hodisalar, qarama-qarshi hodisalar va qo‘shish qoidasi.
probability-rules.body:
Tasodifiy tajriba S elementar hodisalar fazosiga, ya’ni barcha mumkin bo‘lgan natijalar to‘plamiga ega. Hodisa — S ning qism to‘plami. Ehtimolliklar uchta aksiomaga bo‘ysunadi: har qanday ehtimollik 0 va 1 orasida, P(S) = 1, birgalikda yuz bera olmaydigan (birgalikda bo‘lmagan) hodisalar uchun esa ehtimolliklar qo‘shiladi. Barcha natijalar teng ehtimolli bo‘lsa, P(A) = A dagi natijalar soni ÷ S dagi natijalar soni.

Bundan uchta qoida kelib chiqadi. Qarama-qarshi hodisa qoidasi: P(A emas) = 1 − P(A); bu ko‘pincha eng oson yo‘l, masalan P(kamida bitta muvaffaqiyat) = 1 − P(birorta ham muvaffaqiyat yo‘q). Qo‘shish qoidasi: P(A yoki B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A va B); ayirish ikkala hodisaga tegishli natijalarni ikki marta hisoblashning oldini oladi. Birgalikda bo‘lmagan hodisalar uchun P(A va B) = 0.

Misol: 500 xaridor o‘rtasidagi so‘rovnomada 300 kishi mobil bank ilovasidan, 200 kishi kartadan, 120 kishi esa ikkalasidan foydalanadi. Tasodifiy xaridor kamida bittasidan foydalanish ehtimoli P(ilova yoki karta) = 300/500 + 200/500 − 120/500 = 380/500 = 0,76, hech birini ishlatmaslik ehtimoli esa 1 − 0,76 = 0,24.

Asosiy xulosa: elementar hodisalar fazosini aniq yozing, “kamida bitta” savollari uchun qarama-qarshi hodisa qoidasidan foydalaning va birga yuz berishi mumkin bo‘lgan hodisalar ehtimolliklarini qo‘shganda kesishmani ayiring.

conditional-probability.title: Shartli ehtimollik va bog‘liqsizlik
conditional-probability.summary: Yangi ma’lumot ehtimolliklarni qanday o‘zgartiradi va hodisalarning bog‘liqsizligi nimani anglatadi.
conditional-probability.body:
Shartli ehtimollik — B yuz bergan bo‘lsa, A ning ehtimolligi: P(A | B) = P(A va B) ÷ P(B). B ni bilish e’tiborni faqat B ichidagi natijalarga qaratadi. Formulani qayta tuzsak, ko‘paytirish qoidasi hosil bo‘ladi: P(A va B) = P(A | B) × P(B).

Agar birini bilish ikkinchisi haqida hech narsa bermasa, hodisalar bog‘liqsiz: P(A | B) = P(A), yoki unga teng kuchli ravishda P(A va B) = P(A) × P(B). Musbat ehtimollikka ega birgalikda bo‘lmagan hodisalar hech qachon bog‘liqsiz emas: biri yuz bersa, ikkinchisi albatta yuz bermaydi.

Misol: onlayn do‘kon tashrif buyuruvchilarning 40% doimiy mijozlar ekanini, barcha tashrif buyuruvchilarning 15% esa xarid qiladigan doimiy mijozlar ekanini aniqladi. Tashrif buyuruvchi doimiy mijoz bo‘lsa, xarid ehtimoli 0,15 ÷ 0,40 = 0,375. Agar barcha tashrif buyuruvchilarning 20% xarid qilsa, doimiy mijozlar o‘rtachadan ancha ko‘proq xarid qiladi (37,5% va 20%), demak “doimiy mijoz” va “xarid qiladi” hodisalari bog‘liqsiz emas.

Ikki o‘lchovli chastotalar jadvali bu hisoblarni aniq qiladi: bitta shartli ehtimollik uchun katakchani qator yig‘indisiga, ikkinchisi uchun esa ustun yig‘indisiga bo‘ling. P(A | B) ni P(B | A) bilan chalkashtirmang; ular odatda juda farq qiladi va bu Bayes teoremasining mavzusidir.

Asosiy xulosa: P(A | B) = P(A va B) ÷ P(B). Bog‘liqsizlik P(A va B) = P(A)P(B) ni anglatadi va uni taxmin qilmasdan tekshirish kerak.

bayes-theorem.title: Bayes teoremasi
bayes-theorem.summary: Dalillar asosida qarashlarni yangilash va bazaviy ulushni e’tiborsiz qoldirish xatosidan qochish.
bayes-theorem.body:
Bayes teoremasi shartli ehtimollikni teskari aylantiradi: P(A | B) = P(B | A) × P(A) ÷ P(B), bunda maxrajni to‘liq ehtimollik formulasi bilan yoyish mumkin: P(B) = P(B | A)P(A) + P(B | A emas)P(A emas). P(A) — apriori ehtimollik, P(B | A) — haqiqatga o‘xshashlik, P(A | B) esa aposterior ehtimollik, ya’ni B dalilini ko‘rgandan keyin yangilangan qarash.

Misol: karta tranzaksiyalarining 1% firibgarlik. Aniqlash tizimi firibgarlik tranzaksiyalarining 95% ini belgilaydi, ammo qonuniy tranzaksiyalarning 5% ini ham noto‘g‘ri belgilaydi. Tranzaksiya belgilangan bo‘lsa, uning haqiqatan firibgarlik bo‘lish ehtimoli qancha? P(belgi) = 0,95 × 0,01 + 0,05 × 0,99 = 0,0095 + 0,0495 = 0,059. Demak P(firibgarlik | belgi) = 0,0095 ÷ 0,059 ≈ 0,16. Belgilangan tranzaksiyalarning atigi 16% ga yaqini firibgarlikdir.

Kutilmagan natija past bazaviy ulushdan kelib chiqadi. Qonuniy tranzaksiyalar firibgarlikdan ko‘p marta ko‘p bo‘lgani uchun hatto kichik yolg‘on ijobiy daraja ham haqiqiy aniqlashlardan ancha ko‘p yolg‘on signal beradi. Apriori ehtimollikni e’tiborsiz qoldirish bazaviy ulush xatosi deyiladi va u tibbiy testlar, kredit skoringi, spam filtrlash hamda xodimlarni yollashda uchraydi.

Amaliy usul — tabiiy chastotalar: 10 000 ta tranzaksiyani tasavvur qiling. 100 tasi firibgarlik va ulardan 95 tasi belgilanadi; 9 900 tasi qonuniy va ulardan 495 tasi belgilanadi. 590 ta belgidan 95 tasi firibgarlik, ya’ni taxminan 16%.

Asosiy xulosa: aposterior ∝ haqiqatga o‘xshashlik × apriori. Bazaviy ulush past bo‘lsa, ijobiy signal bo‘lsa ham hodisa ehtimoldan uzoq bo‘lib qolishi mumkin.

expected-value-variance.title: Matematik kutilma, dispersiya va standart chetlanish
expected-value-variance.summary: Tasodifiy miqdorni uning uzoq muddatli o‘rtacha qiymati va tarqoqligi orqali tavsiflash.
expected-value-variance.body:
Tasodifiy miqdor tajribaning har bir natijasiga son mos qo‘yadi. Diskret tasodifiy miqdor uchun matematik kutilma uning qiymatlarining ehtimolliklar bilan tortilgan o‘rtachasidir: E[X] = Σ x·P(X = x). Agar tajriba ko‘p marta takrorlansa, bu uzoq muddatli o‘rtacha bo‘ladi. Dispersiya o‘rtacha atrofidagi tarqoqlikni o‘lchaydi: Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²] = E[X²] − (E[X])², standart chetlanish esa σ = √Var(X) bo‘lib, X bilan bir xil birliklarda ifodalanadi.

Misol: kichik investitsiya 0,3 ehtimollik bilan 200, 0,5 ehtimollik bilan 50 foyda, 0,2 ehtimollik bilan esa 100 zarar keltiradi (ming so‘mda). E[X] = 200(0,3) + 50(0,5) − 100(0,2) = 60 + 25 − 20 = 65. E[X²] = 40 000(0,3) + 2 500(0,5) + 10 000(0,2) = 15 250, demak Var(X) = 15 250 − 65² = 11 025 va σ = 105. Investitsiya ijobiy kutilgan daromadga ega, ammo unga nisbatan risk katta.

Foydali qoidalar: E[aX + b] = aE[X] + b va Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). Kutilmalar har doim qo‘shiladi: E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y]. Dispersiyalar faqat bog‘liqsiz (yoki korrelyatsiyalanmagan) miqdorlar uchun qo‘shiladi; umumiy holda Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) + 2Cov(X, Y). Diversifikatsiya ishlaydi, chunki to‘liq korrelyatsiyalanmagan aktivlarni birlashtirish kutilgan daromadga nisbatan dispersiyani kamaytiradi.

Asosiy xulosa: matematik kutilma — markaz, standart chetlanish esa undan odatiy masofa. Moliyada ular kutilgan daromad va riskka aylanadi.

binomial-poisson.title: Binomial va Puasson taqsimotlari
binomial-poisson.summary: Belgilangan sinovlardagi muvaffaqiyatlar va belgilangan oraliqdagi hodisalarni sanash modellari.
binomial-poisson.body:
Binomial taqsimot har birida muvaffaqiyat ehtimoli p bir xil bo‘lgan n ta bog‘liqsiz sinovdagi muvaffaqiyatlar soni X ni sanaydi. Uning ehtimollik formulasi P(X = k) = C(n, k)·pᵏ·(1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ, bu yerda C(n, k) = n! ÷ [k!(n − k)!] qaysi sinovlar muvaffaqiyatli bo‘lishini tanlash usullari soni. Uning o‘rtachasi np, dispersiyasi esa np(1 − p).

Misol: veb-sayt tashrif buyuruvchilarining 20% axborot byulleteniga obuna bo‘ladi. 10 tashrif buyuruvchidan aynan 2 nafari obuna bo‘lish ehtimoli C(10, 2)(0,2)²(0,8)⁸ = 45 × 0,04 × 0,1678 ≈ 0,302. Kutilgan son 10 × 0,2 = 2, dispersiya esa 1,6.

Puasson taqsimoti vaqt yoki fazoning belgilangan oralig‘ida o‘rtacha λ tezlik bilan tasodifiy yuz beradigan hodisalarni sanaydi: P(X = k) = e^(−λ)·λᵏ ÷ k!. Uning o‘rtachasi ham, dispersiyasi ham λ ga teng. U mijozlar kelishini, soatiga qo‘llab-quvvatlash so‘rovlarini, mato metridagi nuqsonlarni yoki oyiga da’volarni modellashtiradi. Misol: call-markaz daqiqasiga o‘rtacha λ = 3 ta qo‘ng‘iroq qabul qiladi. Ma’lum bir daqiqada birorta ham qo‘ng‘iroq bo‘lmaslik ehtimoli e^(−3) ≈ 0,050, aynan 2 ta qo‘ng‘iroq bo‘lish ehtimoli esa e^(−3) × 9 ÷ 2 ≈ 0,224.

n katta va p kichik bo‘lganda Puasson taqsimoti λ = np bilan binomial taqsimotni yaqinlashtiradi. Ikkala taqsimot ham bog‘liqsizlikni nazarda tutadi; agar hodisalar to‘planib qolsa, masalan uzilishdan keyin qo‘ng‘iroqlar keskin ko‘paysa, modellar o‘zgaruvchanlikni kamaytirib ko‘rsatadi.

Asosiy xulosa: belgilangan sinovlar sonidagi muvaffaqiyatlar uchun binomial, doimiy o‘rtacha tezlikdagi hodisalar soni uchun esa Puasson taqsimotidan foydalaning.

normal-distribution.title: Normal taqsimot
normal-distribution.summary: Qo‘ng‘iroqsimon egri chiziq, z-ko‘rsatkichlar va 68–95–99,7 qoidasi.
normal-distribution.body:
Normal taqsimot — o‘rtacha μ va standart chetlanish σ bilan tavsiflanadigan simmetrik, qo‘ng‘iroqsimon uzluksiz taqsimot. Bo‘y uzunligi, o‘lchash xatolari va ko‘plab kichik ta’sirlar o‘rtachasi kabi ko‘plab o‘lchovlar taxminan normal taqsimlangan. Uzluksiz miqdorlar uchun ehtimolliklar zichlik egri chizig‘i ostidagi maydonlardir, shuning uchun bitta qiymat uchun P(X = x) nolga teng va biz oraliqlar haqida so‘raymiz.

Har qanday normal miqdorni z-ko‘rsatkich bilan standartlashtirish mumkin: z = (x − μ) ÷ σ, ya’ni x o‘rtachadan necha standart chetlanish uzoqlikda joylashgani. Standart normal taqsimotda μ = 0 va σ = 1, uning ehtimolliklari jadvallar yoki dasturlar orqali topiladi. Empirik qoida tezkor baholar beradi: qiymatlarning taxminan 68% o‘rtachadan 1σ, 95% 2σ (aniqrog‘i 1,96σ) va 99,7% 3σ masofada joylashgan.

Misol: kuryer yetkazib berish vaqtlari μ = 30 daqiqa va σ = 5 daqiqa bilan normal taqsimlangan. Yetkazib berish 40 daqiqadan oshish ehtimoli P(Z > (40 − 30) ÷ 5) = P(Z > 2) ≈ 0,023, ya’ni taxminan 44 tadan 1 tasi. Vaqtida yetkazib berishni 95% hollarda (bir tomonlama) va’da qilish uchun va’dani μ + 1,645σ ≈ 38,2 daqiqaga belgilang.

Ko‘plab real o‘zgaruvchilar normal emas. Daromadlar, firma o‘lchamlari va moliyaviy daromadlilik ko‘pincha asimmetrik yoki "qalin dumli" bo‘ladi, ya’ni ekstremal qiymatlar normal model bashorat qilganidan ancha tez-tez uchraydi. Normallikni taxmin qilishdan oldin har doim ma’lumotlarni grafikda ko‘ring.

Asosiy xulosa: normal ehtimolliklarni topish uchun z-ko‘rsatkichlarga o‘ting va 68–95–99,7 qoidasini aqliy tekshiruv sifatida ishlating. Asimmetrik yoki qalin dumli ma’lumotlar uchun normallikni taxmin qilmang.

central-limit-theorem.title: Tanlanma taqsimotlari va markaziy limit teoremasi
central-limit-theorem.summary: Nima uchun tanlanma o‘rtachalari taxminan normal taqsimlanadi va aniqlik tanlanma hajmi bilan qanday oshadi.
central-limit-theorem.body:
Tanlanma o‘rtachasi x̄ kabi statistika tanlanmadan tanlanmaga o‘zgaradi. Uning barcha mumkin bo‘lgan tanlanmalar bo‘yicha ehtimollik taqsimoti tanlanma taqsimoti deyiladi. Agar kuzatuvlar o‘rtachasi μ va standart chetlanishi σ bo‘lgan bog‘liqsiz miqdorlar bo‘lsa, E[x̄] = μ (tanlanma o‘rtachasi siljimagan) va uning standart chetlanishi, ya’ni standart xato SE = σ ÷ √n.

Markaziy limit teoremasi (MLT) yetarlicha katta n uchun dastlabki bosh to‘plam shakli qanday bo‘lishidan qat’i nazar, x̄ ning tanlanma taqsimoti taxminan normal bo‘lishini ta’kidlaydi. Keng tarqalgan amaliy qoida — n ≥ 30, ammo kuchli asimmetrik ma’lumotlar ko‘proq kuzatuv talab qiladi. Shuning uchun individual ma’lumotlar normal bo‘lmasa ham, normal taqsimotga asoslangan usullar o‘rtachalar va ulushlar uchun ishlaydi.

Misol: mijoz boshiga kunlik xarajat μ = 60 000 so‘m va σ = 24 000 so‘m bo‘lib, o‘ngga asimmetrik. n = 36 mijozdan iborat tanlanmalar uchun x̄ taxminan normal taqsimlangan, o‘rtachasi 60 000 va SE = 24 000 ÷ 6 = 4 000. Tanlanma o‘rtachasi 68 000 dan oshish ehtimoli P(Z > 2) ≈ 0,023.

SE √n bilan kamaygani uchun aniqlik kamayuvchi samaraga ega: standart xatoni ikki baravar kamaytirish uchun to‘rt baravar ko‘p kuzatuv kerak. p ulush uchun standart xato √[p(1 − p) ÷ n] bo‘lib, bu jamoatchilik so‘rovlaridagi xatolik chegarasining asosidir.

Asosiy xulosa: tanlanma o‘rtachalari μ atrofida σ/√n standart xato bilan joylashadi va katta n uchun taxminan normal taqsimlanadi. Tanlanmani to‘rt baravar oshirish xatoni ikki baravar kamaytiradi.

confidence-intervals.title: Ishonch oraliqlari
confidence-intervals.summary: Bahoni uning noaniqligi bilan birga taqdim etish.
confidence-intervals.body:
Tanlanma o‘rtachasi kabi nuqtaviy baho deyarli hech qachon aynan to‘g‘ri bo‘lmaydi, shuning uchun biz ishonch oralig‘ini taqdim etamiz: baho ± kritik qiymat × standart xato. Katta tanlanmali o‘rtacha uchun 95% oraliq x̄ ± 1,96 × s ÷ √n, bu yerda s — tanlanma standart chetlanishi. Taxminan normal ma’lumotlardan olingan kichik tanlanmalar uchun kritik qiymat n − 1 erkinlik darajali t-taqsimotdan olinadi va u 1,96 dan kattaroq bo‘ladi.

Misol: n = 100 mijoz o‘rtasidagi so‘rovnoma o‘rtacha oylik xarajatni x̄ = 85 000 so‘m, s = 20 000 so‘m deb aniqladi. SE = 20 000 ÷ 10 = 2 000, 95% ishonch oralig‘i esa 85 000 ± 1,96 × 2 000 = 85 000 ± 3 920, ya’ni taxminan 81 100 dan 88 900 so‘mgacha. Ulush uchun p̂ ± 1,96√[p̂(1 − p̂) ÷ n] dan foydalaning: 400 respondentdan 240 nafari mahsulotni afzal ko‘rsa, p̂ = 0,60 va oraliq 0,60 ± 0,048.

Talqin muhim. 95% ishonch darajasi shuni anglatadiki, agar tanlab olishni ko‘p marta takrorlasak, shu usulda tuzilgan oraliqlarning taxminan 95% haqiqiy qiymatni o‘z ichiga oladi. Bu aynan shu oraliq haqiqiy qiymatni 95% ehtimollik bilan o‘z ichiga oladi degani emas. Yuqoriroq ishonch darajasi, o‘zgaruvchanroq ma’lumotlar yoki kichikroq tanlanmalar kengroq oraliq beradi. Xatolik chegarasini ikki baravar kamaytirish uchun tanlanma hajmini to‘rt baravar oshirish kerak.

Asosiy xulosa: baholarni har doim oraliq bilan taqdim eting: baho ± kritik qiymat × SE. Oraliq faqat tanlanma xatosini aks ettiradi, siljigan tanlanmalar yoki noto‘g‘ri o‘lchovlarni emas.

hypothesis-testing.title: Gipotezalarni tekshirish va p-qiymatlar
hypothesis-testing.summary: Nol va muqobil gipotezalar, test statistikalari, p-qiymatlar va ikki turdagi xato.
hypothesis-testing.body:
Gipotezani tekshirish ma’lumotlar standart da’voga qarshi yetarli dalil beradimi, degan savolni beradi. Nol gipoteza H₀ — mavjud holat (masalan, o‘rtacha qadoq og‘irligi 500 g); muqobil gipoteza H₁ — biz dalil izlayotgan narsa (o‘rtacha 500 g emas). Biz ma’lumotlar H₀ dan standart xato birliklarida qanchalik uzoq ekanini o‘lchaydigan test statistikasini hisoblaymiz, z yoki t = (x̄ − μ₀) ÷ SE, so‘ngra p-qiymatni: H₀ to‘g‘ri deb faraz qilinganda kuzatilgan natijalar kabi yoki undan ham ekstremal natijalar olish ehtimolini.

Misol: zavod qoplarda 500 g mahsulot borligini da’vo qiladi. n = 49 qopdan iborat tanlanmada x̄ = 497 g va s = 7 g. SE = 7 ÷ 7 = 1, demak t ≈ (497 − 500) ÷ 1 = −3. Ikki tomonlama p-qiymat taxminan 0,004. Odatiy α = 0,05 ahamiyatlilik darajasida p < α, shuning uchun H₀ ni rad etamiz: dalillar qoplar to‘liq to‘ldirilmayotganini ko‘rsatadi.

Ikki xil xato bo‘lishi mumkin. I tur xato to‘g‘ri H₀ ni rad etadi (yolg‘on signal) va uning ehtimoli α ga teng. II tur xato noto‘g‘ri H₀ ni rad etmaydi (o‘tkazib yuborilgan ta’sir), ehtimoli β; testning quvvati 1 − β. Kattaroq tanlanmalar quvvatni oshiradi. p-qiymat H₀ ning to‘g‘ri bo‘lish ehtimoli emas, "rad etmaslik" esa H₀ to‘g‘ri ekanining isboti emas; bu dalillar yetarli bo‘lmaganini anglatadi.

Asosiy xulosa: ma’lumotlarga qarashdan oldin H₀ va H₁ ni belgilang, test statistikasi va p-qiymatni hisoblang hamda α bilan solishtiring. p-qiymat bilan birga ta’sir kattaligi va ishonch oralig‘ini ham taqdim eting.

ab-testing.title: Ikki guruhni taqqoslash: A/B test
ab-testing.summary: O‘zgarish konversiya darajasini haqiqatan yaxshilaganini ikki ulushli z-test yordamida tekshirish.
ab-testing.body:
A/B test foydalanuvchilarni tasodifiy ravishda nazorat versiyasi (A) va variantga (B) taqsimlaydi hamda konversiya darajasi kabi natijani solishtiradi. Tasodifiy taqsimlash sababiy xulosa chiqarishga imkon beradi: tasodifdan tashqari guruhlar o‘rtasidagi yagona tizimli farq — sinovdan o‘tkazilayotgan o‘zgarishdir.

Konversiya darajalari uchun ikki ulushli z-testdan foydalaning. Umumlashtirilgan ulush p = (x_A + x_B) ÷ (n_A + n_B) bo‘lganda standart xato SE = √[p(1 − p)(1/n_A + 1/n_B)] va z = (p̂_B − p̂_A) ÷ SE.

Misol: A versiya 4 000 tashrif buyuruvchidan 200 tasini (5,0%), B versiya esa 4 000 dan 260 tasini (6,5%) konversiya qiladi. Umumlashtirilgan daraja 460 ÷ 8 000 = 5,75%, demak SE = √[0,0575 × 0,9425 × (2 ÷ 4 000)] ≈ 0,0052. Unda z = 0,015 ÷ 0,0052 ≈ 2,88 va ikki tomonlama p-qiymat taxminan 0,004. 1,5 foiz punktlik o‘sish (nisbiy 30%) α = 0,05 darajasida statistik ahamiyatli, farq uchun 95% oraliq esa taxminan 0,5 dan 2,5 punktgacha.

Yaxshi amaliyot: aniqlashga arziydigan eng kichik ta’sir uchun quvvat hisobi yordamida tanlanma hajmini oldindan belgilang; p 0,05 dan pastga tushishi bilan testni erta to‘xtatmang ("mo‘ralash" yolg‘on ijobiy natijalarni ko‘paytiradi); testni to‘liq haftalik sikllar davomida o‘tkazing; foydalanuvchilarning guruhlarga taqsimlanishi rejaga mos kelishini tekshiring.

Asosiy xulosa: tasodifiy taqsimlang, tanlanma hajmini oldindan belgilang va ikki ulushli z-testdan foydalaning. O‘sishni shunchaki "ahamiyatli" deb emas, ishonch oralig‘i bilan taqdim eting.

significance-pitfalls.title: Xatolar: ko‘p sonli testlar va amaliy ahamiyat
significance-pitfalls.summary: Nima uchun ko‘p sonli testlar yolg‘on kashfiyotlarga olib keladi va nima uchun statistik ahamiyatli degani muhim degani emas.
significance-pitfalls.body:
Haqiqiy ta’sir bo‘lmaganda α = 0,05 darajasida bitta test o‘tkazsangiz, yolg‘on ijobiy natija ehtimoli 5% ni tashkil etadi. 20 ta bog‘liqsiz test o‘tkazsangiz, kamida bitta yolg‘on ijobiy natija ehtimoli 1 − 0,95²⁰ ≈ 64%. Ko‘plab ko‘rsatkichlar, segmentlar yoki variantlarni sinab, faqat ahamiyatlilarini e’lon qilish (ba’zan p-hacking yoki ma’lumotlarni titkilash deyiladi) soxta topilmalarni deyarli kafolatlaydi. Yechimlar: asosiy ko‘rsatkichni oldindan ro‘yxatdan o‘tkazish, Bonferroni tuzatmasi (m ta test uchun α ÷ m dan foydalaning, 20 ta test uchun 0,0025) va kutilmagan natijalarni yangi tanlanmada tasdiqlash.

Statistik ahamiyat amaliy ahamiyat bilan ham bir xil emas. Juda katta tanlanmada konversiyadagi 0,01 foiz punktlik farq yuqori darajada ahamiyatli bo‘lishi, lekin tijorat jihatdan befoyda bo‘lishi mumkin. Kichik tanlanmada esa muhim ta’sir ahamiyatlilikka erishmasligi mumkin. Har doim ta’sir kattaligi va uning ishonch oralig‘iga qarang hamda o‘zgarish qarorlar, daromad yoki farovonlik uchun ahamiyatlimi, deb so‘rang.

Boshqa keng tarqalgan tuzoqlar: tanlov siljishi (faqat qolgan mijozlarni tahlil qilish), omon qolganlik siljishi (faqat muvaffaqiyatli firmalarni o‘rganish), Simpson paradoksi (ma’lumotlar guruhlarga bo‘linganda teskari o‘zgaradigan tendensiya) va o‘rtachaga qaytish (ekstremal natijalardan keyin odatda oddiyroq natijalar keladi, bu esa aralashuvni samarasiz bo‘lsa ham samarali qilib ko‘rsatishi mumkin).

Asosiy xulosa: testlaringizni cheklang va oldindan belgilang, ko‘p sonli taqqoslashlar uchun tuzatma kiriting hamda natijalarni faqat p-qiymatlar bo‘yicha emas, ta’sir kattaligi va ishonch oraliqlari bo‘yicha baholang.

correlation.title: Kovariatsiya va korrelyatsiya
correlation.summary: Chiziqli bog‘liqlikning kuchi va yo‘nalishini o‘lchash.
correlation.body:
Kovariatsiya ikki o‘zgaruvchi birga o‘zgarishini o‘lchaydi: Cov(X, Y) = (x − x̄)(y − ȳ) ning o‘rtachasi. O‘rtachadan yuqori x odatda o‘rtachadan yuqori y bilan birga kelsa, u musbat, ular qarama-qarshi yo‘nalishda o‘zgarsa, manfiy bo‘ladi. Uning kattaligi o‘lchov birliklariga bog‘liq, shuning uchun uni alohida talqin qilish qiyin.

Korrelyatsiya koeffitsienti kovariatsiyani standartlashtiradi: r = Cov(X, Y) ÷ (s_X·s_Y). U har doim −1 va +1 orasida bo‘ladi. +1 yoki −1 ga yaqin qiymatlar kuchli chiziqli bog‘liqlikni, 0 ga yaqin qiymatlar esa zaif chiziqli bog‘liqlikni bildiradi. r o‘lchov birligiga ega emas, X va Y ga nisbatan simmetrik va birliklarni, masalan so‘mdan dollarga o‘zgartirishdan ta’sirlanmaydi.

Uchta ogohlantirish. Birinchidan, korrelyatsiya faqat chiziqli bog‘liqlikni o‘lchaydi: mukammal U shaklidagi bog‘liqlikda r = 0 bo‘lishi mumkin, shuning uchun har doim tarqalish diagrammasini chizing. Ikkinchidan, bir nechta chetga chiqqan qiymat korrelyatsiyani yaratishi yoki yo‘q qilishi mumkin. Uchinchidan, eng muhimi, korrelyatsiya sababiy bog‘liqlik emas. Muzqaymoq sotuvi va suvga cho‘kish holatlari korrelyatsiyalangan, chunki ikkalasi ham issiq havoda oshadi — bu chalkashtiruvchi o‘zgaruvchi. Politsiyasi ko‘proq shaharlarda ko‘pincha jinoyat ham ko‘proq, qisman jinoyat yuqori bo‘lgan joyga ko‘proq politsiya yuborilgani uchun — bu teskari sababiyatdir.

Asosiy xulosa: r chiziqli bog‘liqlikning kuchi va yo‘nalishini −1 dan 1 gacha shkalada o‘lchaydi. Ma’lumotlarni grafikda ko‘ring, chetga chiqqan qiymatlarga e’tibor bering va faqat korrelyatsiyadan sababiyat haqida xulosa chiqarmang.

simple-linear-regression.title: Oddiy chiziqli regressiya
simple-linear-regression.summary: Eng kichik kvadratlar usuli bilan to‘g‘ri chiziq o‘tkazing, uning qiyaligini talqin qiling va moslikni R² bilan o‘lchang.
simple-linear-regression.body:
Oddiy chiziqli regressiya y ni x ning to‘g‘ri chiziqli funksiyasi va xato yig‘indisi sifatida modellashtiradi: y = a + b·x + e. Eng kichik kvadratlar usuli (EKKU) a va b ni qoldiqlar kvadratlari yig‘indisini minimallashtiradigan qilib tanlaydi; qoldiq — haqiqiy va bashorat qilingan qiymat orasidagi farq. Yechim: b = Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) ÷ Σ(x − x̄)² va a = ȳ − b·x̄, shuning uchun o‘tkazilgan chiziq har doim o‘rtachalar nuqtasidan o‘tadi.

Misol: besh oy uchun reklama xarajati x (million so‘m) va sotuv y (million so‘m): (1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 4), (4, 7), (5, 8). Bu yerda x̄ = 3 va ȳ = 5,4. Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) = 12 va Σ(x − x̄)² = 10, demak b = 1,2 va a = 5,4 − 1,2 × 3 = 1,8. O‘tkazilgan chiziq ŷ = 1,8 + 1,2x: reklamaga sarflangan har bir qo‘shimcha million so‘m 1,2 million so‘m ko‘proq sotuv bilan bog‘liq.

R², determinatsiya koeffitsienti, y dagi o‘zgaruvchanlikning chiziq tushuntirgan ulushi: R² = 1 − (qoldiqlar kvadratlari yig‘indisi ÷ umumiy kvadratlar yig‘indisi). Bu yerda umumiy kvadratlar yig‘indisi 17,2, tushuntirilgan qism esa 14,4, demak R² ≈ 0,84. Oddiy regressiyada R² = r².

Moslikka ishonishdan oldin qoldiqlarni tekshiring: ular x ga nisbatan hech qanday qonuniyat ko‘rsatmasligi, taxminan doimiy tarqoqlikka ega bo‘lishi va ekstremal chetga chiqqan qiymatlarsiz bo‘lishi kerak. b uchun standart xato ishonch oralig‘i va haqiqiy qiyalik nolga tengligini tekshiradigan t-testni beradi. x ning kuzatilgan oralig‘idan ancha tashqaridagi bashoratlar (ekstrapolyatsiya) ishonchsiz.

Asosiy xulosa: EKKU b = Cov(x, y)/Var(x) va a = ȳ − b·x̄ ni beradi. Qiyalikni x bir birlikka o‘zgarganda y ning tegishli o‘zgarishi sifatida talqin qiling va unga tayanishdan oldin qoldiqlarni tekshiring.

multiple-regression-causality.title: Ko‘p omilli regressiya va sababiy xulosa
multiple-regression-causality.summary: Bir vaqtning o‘zida bir nechta omilni nazorat qiling, koeffitsientlarni to‘g‘ri talqin qiling va tushirib qoldirilgan o‘zgaruvchi siljishini taniy oling.
multiple-regression-causality.body:
Ko‘p omilli regressiya bir nechta tushuntiruvchi o‘zgaruvchini o‘z ichiga oladi: y = b₀ + b₁x₁ + b₂x₂ + … + e. Har bir bⱼ koeffitsienti modelga kiritilgan boshqa o‘zgaruvchilar o‘zgarmas bo‘lganda xⱼ va y o‘rtasidagi bog‘liqlikni o‘lchaydi. Masalan, ta’lim yillari va ish tajribasi yillari bilan ish haqi regressiyasida ta’lim koeffitsienti bir xil tajribaga ega odamlarni taqqoslaydi.

Foydali spetsifikatsiyalar: soxta (dummy) o‘zgaruvchilar (0/1) mintaqa yoki jins kabi toifalarni qamrab oladi; log-log model ln y = b₀ + b₁ ln x da b₁ elastiklik bo‘ladi; log-daraja model ln y = b₀ + b₁x da esa x ning bir birlikka oshishi y ni taxminan 100·b₁ foizga o‘zgartiradi. Tuzatilgan R² moslikni yaxshilamaydigan o‘zgaruvchilarni qo‘shganlik uchun jarima qo‘llaydi.

Talqin uchun asosiy xavf — tushirib qoldirilgan o‘zgaruvchi siljishi. Agar y ga ta’sir qiladigan va modelga kiritilgan x bilan korrelyatsiyalangan o‘zgaruvchi tushirib qoldirilsa, x koeffitsienti uning ta’sirini o‘ziga singdiradi. Agar qobiliyat tushirib qoldirilsa, ta’limdan olinadigan daromad oshirib ko‘rsatiladi, chunki qobiliyatliroq odamlar ko‘proq ta’lim olishga va ko‘proq ishlashga moyil. Multikollinearlik, ya’ni tushuntiruvchi o‘zgaruvchilar bir-biri bilan kuchli korrelyatsiyalanganda, koeffitsientlarni siljitmaydi, lekin ularni noaniq qiladi.

Bog‘liqlikdan sababiyatga o‘tish uchun iqtisodchilar tadqiqot dizaynlariga tayanadi: tasodifiy tajribalar, tabiiy tajribalar, farqlar farqi usuli (ta’sir ko‘rsatilgan va ko‘rsatilmagan guruhlar o‘rtasida vaqt bo‘yicha o‘zgarishlarni taqqoslash), instrumental o‘zgaruvchilar va regressiya uzilishi. Ularning har biri mavjud bo‘lmagan tajriba o‘rniga "go‘yo tasodifiy" o‘zgaruvchanlikdan foydalanadi.

Asosiy xulosa: ko‘p omilli regressiya koeffitsienti — boshqa kiritilgan o‘zgaruvchilar o‘zgarmas bo‘lgandagi xususiy ta’sir. Ishonchli tadqiqot dizaynisiz tushirib qoldirilgan o‘zgaruvchilar uni sababiy ta’sir emas, balki korrelyatsiyaga aylantirishi mumkin.

topics.title: Startup Strategy & Unit Economics
topics.description: Go from a customer problem to a business that makes money on every customer: validate demand, size the market, design a revenue model, master CAC, LTV and contribution margin, and plan growth, runway and fundraising.

modules.title: Problem, customer and market
modules.summary: Find a real problem, confirm that customers will pay to solve it, and estimate how big the opportunity is.

lessons.title: Customer discovery and problem validation
lessons.summary: Interview customers about their past behavior to find problems worth solving.
lessons.body:
Most startups fail not because they cannot build a product but because they build something too few people want. Customer discovery is the disciplined process of testing your assumptions about who the customer is, what problem they have and how they solve it today, before investing heavily in a solution.

Good discovery interviews ask about past behavior, not hypothetical opinions. Instead of “Would you use an app that tracks your shop's inventory?”, ask “Tell me about the last time you ran out of stock. What did you do? What did it cost you? What have you tried to fix it?” People are polite about ideas but honest about their own history. Signs of a real problem include customers who already spend time or money on workarounds, such as spreadsheets, extra staff or paid tools, and who describe the pain with specific numbers.

A useful lens is jobs to be done: customers “hire” a product to make progress in a specific situation. A small shop owner does not want software; they want to stop losing sales because popular items run out. Write down your riskiest assumptions, then run 15 to 20 interviews with people in your target segment and look for repeated patterns. Stronger evidence than words is commitment: a pre-order, a signed letter of intent or a paid pilot.

Key takeaway: validate the problem before building the solution. Ask about past behavior, look for existing spending on workarounds, and seek commitments, not compliments.

lessons.title: Market sizing: TAM, SAM and SOM
lessons.summary: Estimate the size of the opportunity bottom-up and sanity-check it top-down.
lessons.body:
Investors and founders need to know whether a market is big enough to support a substantial company. Three nested numbers are used. The total addressable market (TAM) is total annual revenue if every possible customer bought your product. The serviceable available market (SAM) is the part you can actually reach with your product, channels and geography. The serviceable obtainable market (SOM) is the share you can realistically win in the next few years.

Bottom-up sizing is more credible than top-down: count customers and multiply by what each will pay. Example with illustrative numbers: suppose there are 40,000 cafés and restaurants nationally, and your inventory software costs 500,000 UZS per month. TAM = 40,000 × 500,000 × 12 = 240 billion UZS per year. If you can initially serve only the 15,000 venues in two large cities, SAM = 90 billion UZS. Winning 5% of SAM within three years gives SOM = 4.5 billion UZS of annual revenue.

Top-down sizing starts from an industry statistic and takes percentages (“the restaurant market is X; software is 1% of costs”). It is useful as a cross-check but easy to inflate. State your assumptions explicitly so others can challenge them, and watch for the classic error of claiming a tiny share of an enormous market without explaining how you will win it.

Key takeaway: build market size from the bottom up (customers × price × frequency), narrow from TAM to SAM to SOM, and make every assumption visible.

lessons.title: MVPs and product-market fit
lessons.summary: Test your riskiest assumptions with the smallest possible product and learn to recognise product-market fit.
lessons.body:
A minimum viable product (MVP) is the smallest thing you can build to test your riskiest assumption with real customers. It is an experiment, not a cheap version of the final product. Forms include a landing page that measures sign-ups, a “concierge” service delivered manually behind a simple interface, or a single core feature used by a handful of paying customers. The loop is build, measure, learn: define what result would prove you wrong before you launch, then measure and decide whether to persevere or pivot.

Product-market fit means a product satisfies a strong market demand so well that growth is pulled by customers rather than pushed by the team. Signals include retention curves that flatten (a stable share of each cohort keeps using the product month after month), organic word-of-mouth growth, customers who complain loudly when the product breaks, and sales cycles that get shorter. A widely used survey test asks users how they would feel if they could no longer use the product; when roughly 40% or more answer “very disappointed”, fit is likely.

Before product-market fit, the priority is learning: talk to users weekly and change the product quickly. After fit, the priority shifts to scaling acquisition, operations and the team. Scaling marketing spend before fit usually just buys customers who churn.

Key takeaway: use MVPs as experiments with predefined success criteria. Look for flattening retention and pull from customers before pouring money into growth.

modules.title: Business model and unit economics
modules.summary: How the business makes money and whether each customer is profitable.

lessons.title: Revenue models and pricing
lessons.summary: Subscriptions, transactions, marketplaces and usage-based pricing, and how to choose a price.
lessons.body:
A revenue model describes how a business captures value. Common models include subscriptions (a recurring monthly or annual fee, as in software-as-a-service), transactional sales (one-off purchases), marketplaces (taking a commission, or take rate, on transactions between buyers and sellers), usage-based pricing (paying per message, gigabyte or ride), advertising, and freemium (a free tier that converts a small share of users to paid plans).

For a marketplace, revenue = gross merchandise value (GMV) × take rate. A delivery platform processing 10 billion UZS of orders a month with a 15% take rate earns 1.5 billion UZS in revenue, not 10 billion. Confusing GMV with revenue is a common error in pitch decks.

Pricing has three anchors. Cost-plus pricing adds a markup to unit cost, which is simple but ignores customer value. Competitor-based pricing matches or undercuts alternatives. Value-based pricing starts from the economic value the customer gets: if your software saves a shop 2 million UZS a month in lost sales and staff time, a price of 400,000 UZS leaves the customer clearly better off. Tiered plans (basic, pro, enterprise) let different customer segments self-select, which captures more of the value spread.

Key takeaway: choose a revenue model that matches how customers get value, report revenue rather than GMV, and price from customer value, using costs as the floor and competitors as a reference.

lessons.title: Contribution margin and break-even
lessons.summary: How much each sale contributes to fixed costs, and how many sales you need to break even.
lessons.body:
Contribution margin per unit is price minus variable cost per unit: the amount each sale contributes toward fixed costs and then profit. Variable costs scale with each unit sold (ingredients, packaging, payment fees, delivery, sales commissions); fixed costs do not (rent, salaried staff, software subscriptions). The contribution margin ratio is contribution margin ÷ price.

Break-even volume = fixed costs ÷ contribution margin per unit. Example: a meal-kit startup sells kits at 80,000 UZS. Ingredients, packaging, delivery and payment fees total 56,000 UZS, so each kit contributes 24,000 UZS (a 30% margin). With monthly fixed costs of 120 million UZS, break-even is 120,000,000 ÷ 24,000 = 5,000 kits per month. To earn a target profit of 30 million UZS, the startup needs (120 + 30) million ÷ 24,000 = 6,250 kits.

Contribution margin reveals whether growth helps or hurts. If the margin is negative, every extra sale deepens losses and scale cannot fix the business; discounts, free delivery and subsidized promotions often hide this. Improving unit economics means raising price, lowering variable cost (better supplier terms, route density in delivery, automation) or shifting the mix toward higher-margin products. Operating leverage, a high share of fixed costs, makes profits grow quickly above break-even but makes losses steep below it.

Key takeaway: know your contribution margin per unit and your break-even volume. Never try to scale a product whose contribution margin is negative.

lessons.title: CAC, LTV and payback period
lessons.summary: The core metrics that tell you whether acquiring customers creates or destroys value.
lessons.body:
Customer acquisition cost (CAC) is total sales and marketing spend in a period divided by the number of new customers acquired: if you spend 50 million UZS and win 100 customers, CAC = 500,000 UZS. Include salaries of sales staff and agency fees, not just advertising, and compute CAC by channel because channels differ greatly.

Customer lifetime value (LTV) is the gross profit you expect from a customer over the whole relationship. For a subscription business with monthly churn rate c, the average customer lifetime is 1 ÷ c months, so LTV = (ARPU × gross margin) ÷ churn, where ARPU is average revenue per user per month. Example: ARPU = 100,000 UZS, gross margin = 70% and monthly churn = 4%. LTV = 70,000 ÷ 0.04 = 1,750,000 UZS.

Two ratios summarize the health of growth. LTV ÷ CAC = 1,750,000 ÷ 500,000 = 3.5; a common benchmark is at least 3, meaning each som of acquisition spend returns three som of gross profit. The CAC payback period is CAC ÷ (ARPU × gross margin) = 500,000 ÷ 70,000 ≈ 7 months: the time to recover acquisition spending. Shorter payback means less cash is tied up in growth, which matters a great deal for early-stage companies with limited funds.

Be careful: LTV estimates are very sensitive to churn (halving churn doubles LTV), young companies have little data on long-term retention, and LTV should use gross profit, not revenue. Many startups have looked healthy on paper because they used revenue-based LTV and blended CAC that hid expensive paid channels.

Key takeaway: LTV = ARPU × gross margin ÷ churn; aim for LTV/CAC of 3 or more and a payback period of about a year or less, computed by channel and with conservative churn.

lessons.title: Cohorts, churn and net revenue retention
lessons.summary: Track groups of customers over time to see whether the business is really improving.
lessons.body:
Averages across all customers can hide what is happening. Cohort analysis groups customers by the month they joined and follows each group over time. A retention table shows, for example, that of customers who joined in January, 100% were active in month 0, 62% in month 1, 48% in month 3 and 45% in month 6. If later cohorts retain better than earlier ones, the product is improving; if the curve keeps falling toward zero, the business has a leaky bucket that marketing spend cannot fill.

Customer churn is the share of customers lost in a period: churn = customers lost ÷ customers at the start of the period. A monthly churn of 5% sounds small but means losing about 46% of customers in a year (1 − 0.95¹² ≈ 0.46). Revenue churn can differ from customer churn when large and small customers behave differently.

Net revenue retention (NRR) measures how revenue from an existing cohort changes, including upgrades: NRR = (starting recurring revenue + expansion − contraction − churned revenue) ÷ starting recurring revenue. Example: a cohort starts the year at 100 million UZS of monthly recurring revenue, adds 15 million from upgrades, loses 5 million from downgrades and 8 million from cancellations. NRR = (100 + 15 − 5 − 8) ÷ 100 = 102%. Above 100%, existing customers grow revenue even with zero new sales, which is a hallmark of the strongest subscription businesses.

Key takeaway: analyse retention by cohort, convert monthly churn to annual terms to feel its true weight, and track net revenue retention as the clearest sign of durable growth.

modules.title: Growth, runway and fundraising
modules.summary: Choose growth channels, manage cash burn and understand how equity financing and dilution work.

lessons.title: Growth channels and funnels
lessons.summary: Map the customer journey, find the bottleneck, and understand virality.
lessons.body:
A growth funnel breaks the customer journey into stages so you can see where people drop off. A popular framework is AARRR: acquisition (people arrive), activation (they have a good first experience), retention (they come back), referral (they bring others) and revenue (they pay). Measure the conversion rate between each stage. Example: 10,000 visitors → 1,500 sign-ups (15%) → 600 activated users (40%) → 240 paying customers (40%). Improving the weakest step usually has the biggest effect; doubling activation from 40% to 80% doubles paying customers without spending more on acquisition.

Growth channels include paid ads, search engine optimization, content, partnerships, direct sales, marketplaces and app stores, and referral programs. Early on, find one or two channels that work and go deep rather than spreading thinly; each channel's CAC and scalability differ widely. Messaging apps, social networks and local influencers can be especially efficient channels in markets where they dominate online life.

Virality is measured by the viral coefficient K = invitations sent per user × conversion rate of an invitation. If each user invites 5 people and 10% join, K = 0.5: every 100 users bring in 50 more, then 25, and so on, multiplying organic growth by 1 ÷ (1 − K) = 2. Only K > 1 produces self-sustaining exponential growth, which is rare. Cycle time, how fast invitations convert, matters as much as K.

Key takeaway: measure your funnel stage by stage and fix the biggest bottleneck first, concentrate on the channels with the best CAC, and treat virality as an amplifier rather than a plan.

lessons.title: Burn rate, runway and cash planning
lessons.summary: How long the company can survive on the cash it has, and how to plan around it.
lessons.body:
Startups often lose money for years while they build and grow, so cash, not profit, determines survival. Gross burn is total monthly cash spending; net burn is cash spending minus cash coming in. Runway = cash in the bank ÷ net burn. Example: with 3.6 billion UZS in the bank and a net burn of 300 million UZS a month, runway is 12 months.

Plan fundraising around runway. Raising a new round typically takes several months from first meetings to money in the bank, so many founders start when they still have 6 to 9 months of runway left. Running out of cash before reaching the next milestone forces bad terms or closure. A useful question is whether the company is “default alive”: at current growth rates and costs, would it reach profitability before the money runs out?

Cash planning uses a simple monthly model: starting cash + cash inflows − cash outflows = ending cash. Revenue is not the same as cash; customers may pay late, and annual prepayments bring cash forward. Build scenarios (base, upside and downside) and identify the levers you would pull in a downturn, such as pausing hiring, cutting the least efficient marketing channels or renegotiating contracts. Cutting costs early is far less painful than cutting them when only two months of cash remain.

Key takeaway: runway = cash ÷ net burn. Track it monthly, start fundraising with at least six months left, and know which costs you would cut if growth disappoints.

lessons.title: Fundraising, valuation and dilution
lessons.summary: Pre-money and post-money valuation, ownership after a round, and common early-stage instruments.
lessons.body:
Equity financing means selling a share of the company to investors in exchange for cash. Two valuations matter. Pre-money valuation is the agreed value before the new money; post-money valuation = pre-money + new investment. The investors' ownership is investment ÷ post-money.

Example: a startup agrees a pre-money valuation of $2 million and raises $500,000. Post-money is $2.5 million, so the investors own 500,000 ÷ 2,500,000 = 20%. The founders, who owned 100%, now own 80%. This is dilution: their percentage falls, but if the money helps the company grow, 80% of a larger company can be worth much more than 100% of a smaller one. Investors usually also require an employee option pool (often 10–15%) to be created before the round, which dilutes the founders further.

Over several rounds, dilution compounds. If founders give up 20% at seed, 20% at Series A and 15% at Series B, they keep 0.8 × 0.8 × 0.85 ≈ 54% of their original stake. A capitalization table (cap table) tracks every holder's shares after each round.

Early rounds often use instruments that delay setting a price, such as convertible notes or SAFEs (simple agreements for future equity). They convert into shares at the next priced round, typically with a valuation cap or a discount that rewards early risk. Beyond valuation, read the terms: liquidation preferences, board seats and protective provisions can matter more than the headline price. Alternatives to equity include revenue-based financing, grants, bank loans and bootstrapping from customer revenue.

Key takeaway: post-money = pre-money + investment, and investor ownership = investment ÷ post-money. Model dilution across future rounds and pay close attention to terms, not just valuation.

problem-market.summary: Haqiqiy muammoni toping, mijozlar uni hal qilish uchun pul to‘lashini tasdiqlang va imkoniyat qanchalik katta ekanini baholang.

unit-economics.summary: Biznes qanday pul ishlaydi va har bir mijoz foydali ekanmi.
