growth-fundraising.summary: O‘sish kanallarini tanlang, pul sarfini boshqaring va kapital orqali moliyalashtirish hamda ulush suyultirilishi qanday ishlashini tushuning.

customer-discovery.title: Mijozlarni o‘rganish va muammoni tasdiqlash
customer-discovery.summary: Hal qilishga arziydigan muammolarni topish uchun mijozlardan ularning o‘tmishdagi xatti-harakatlari haqida so‘rang.
customer-discovery.body:
Ko‘pchilik startaplar mahsulot yarata olmagani uchun emas, balki juda kam odam xohlaydigan narsani yaratgani uchun muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchraydi. Mijozlarni o‘rganish — yechimga katta mablag‘ sarflashdan oldin mijoz kim, uning qanday muammosi bor va u bugun uni qanday hal qilayotgani haqidagi farazlaringizni tizimli tekshirish jarayoni.

Yaxshi suhbatlar faraziy fikrlar haqida emas, o‘tmishdagi xatti-harakatlar haqida so‘raydi. "Do‘koningiz zaxirasini kuzatadigan ilovadan foydalanarmidingiz?" deyish o‘rniga "Oxirgi marta mahsulot tugab qolganini aytib bering. Nima qildingiz? Bu sizga qanchaga tushdi? Buni tuzatish uchun nimalarni sinab ko‘rdingiz?" deb so‘rang. Odamlar g‘oyalar haqida xushmuomala, lekin o‘z tarixi haqida halol bo‘ladi. Haqiqiy muammo belgilari: mijozlar allaqachon jadval, qo‘shimcha xodim yoki pullik vositalar kabi vaqtinchalik yechimlarga vaqt yoki pul sarflayapti va og‘riqni aniq raqamlar bilan tasvirlaydi.

Foydali yondashuv — "bajariladigan ishlar" (jobs to be done): mijozlar ma’lum vaziyatda oldinga siljish uchun mahsulotni "yollaydi". Kichik do‘kon egasi dasturiy ta’minotni xohlamaydi; u ommabop mahsulotlar tugab qolgani sababli sotuvni yo‘qotishni to‘xtatmoqchi. Eng xavfli farazlaringizni yozib chiqing, so‘ng maqsadli segmentdagi odamlar bilan 15–20 ta suhbat o‘tkazing va takrorlanuvchi qonuniyatlarni izlang. So‘zlardan kuchliroq dalil — majburiyat: oldindan buyurtma, imzolangan niyat xati yoki pullik sinov loyihasi.

Asosiy xulosa: yechimni yaratishdan oldin muammoni tasdiqlang. O‘tmishdagi xatti-harakatlar haqida so‘rang, vaqtinchalik yechimlarga mavjud xarajatlarni izlang va maqtovlar emas, majburiyatlar izlang.

market-sizing.title: Bozor hajmini baholash: TAM, SAM va SOM
market-sizing.summary: Imkoniyat hajmini pastdan yuqoriga baholang va uni yuqoridan pastga usuli bilan tekshiring.
market-sizing.body:
Investorlar va asoschilar bozor yirik kompaniyani ko‘tara oladigan darajada katta ekanini bilishlari kerak. Buning uchun bir-biriga joylashgan uchta ko‘rsatkichdan foydalaniladi. Umumiy manzilli bozor (TAM) — barcha mumkin bo‘lgan mijozlar mahsulotingizni sotib olganda yillik umumiy tushum. Xizmat ko‘rsatish mumkin bo‘lgan bozor (SAM) — mahsulotingiz, kanallaringiz va hududingiz bilan haqiqatan yetib borishingiz mumkin bo‘lgan qism. Erishish mumkin bo‘lgan bozor (SOM) — keyingi bir necha yilda real egallashingiz mumkin bo‘lgan ulush.

Pastdan yuqoriga baholash yuqoridan pastga baholashdan ishonchliroq: mijozlarni sanang va har biri to‘laydigan summaga ko‘paytiring. Shartli raqamlar bilan misol: mamlakatda 40 000 ta kafe va restoran bor deb faraz qilaylik, zaxira dasturingiz esa oyiga 500 000 so‘m turadi. TAM = 40 000 × 500 000 × 12 = yiliga 240 milliard so‘m. Agar dastlab faqat ikki yirik shahardagi 15 000 ta muassasaga xizmat ko‘rsata olsangiz, SAM = 90 milliard so‘m. Uch yil ichida SAM ning 5% ini egallash SOM = 4,5 milliard so‘m yillik tushumni beradi.

Yuqoridan pastga baholash tarmoq statistikasidan boshlanib, foizlarni oladi ("restoran bozori X ga teng; dasturiy ta’minot xarajatlarning 1% ini tashkil etadi"). U o‘zaro tekshiruv sifatida foydali, lekin uni oshirib yuborish oson. Boshqalar e’tiroz bildira olishi uchun farazlaringizni aniq ko‘rsating va ulkan bozorning kichik ulushini qanday egallashingizni tushuntirmasdan da’vo qilish kabi klassik xatodan saqlaning.

Asosiy xulosa: bozor hajmini pastdan yuqoriga quring (mijozlar × narx × chastota), TAM dan SAM va SOM ga toraytiring hamda har bir farazni ko‘rinadigan qiling.

mvp-product-market-fit.title: MVP va mahsulotning bozorga mosligi
mvp-product-market-fit.summary: Eng xavfli farazlaringizni eng kichik mahsulot bilan sinab ko‘ring va mahsulotning bozorga mosligini taniy olishni o‘rganing.
mvp-product-market-fit.body:
Minimal hayotiy mahsulot (MVP) — eng xavfli farazingizni real mijozlar bilan sinash uchun yaratish mumkin bo‘lgan eng kichik narsa. Bu yakuniy mahsulotning arzon versiyasi emas, balki tajribadir. Uning shakllari: ro‘yxatdan o‘tishlarni o‘lchaydigan landing sahifa, oddiy interfeys ortida qo‘lda ko‘rsatiladigan "konsyerj" xizmati yoki bir nechta pullik mijoz foydalanadigan yagona asosiy funksiya. Sikl — yaratish, o‘lchash, o‘rganish: ishga tushirishdan oldin qanday natija sizni noto‘g‘ri ekaningizni isbotlashini belgilang, so‘ng o‘lchang va davom etish yoki yo‘nalishni o‘zgartirish (pivot) haqida qaror qabul qiling.

Mahsulotning bozorga mosligi mahsulot kuchli bozor talabini shunchalik yaxshi qondirishini anglatadiki, o‘sishni jamoa itarmaydi, balki mijozlar tortadi. Belgilar: tekislanadigan saqlab qolish egri chiziqlari (har bir kogortaning barqaror ulushi mahsulotdan oydan-oyga foydalanishda davom etadi), og‘zaki tavsiya orqali organik o‘sish, mahsulot buzilganda baland ovozda shikoyat qiladigan mijozlar va qisqarib borayotgan sotuv sikllari. Keng qo‘llaniladigan so‘rovnoma testi foydalanuvchilardan mahsulotdan boshqa foydalana olmasalar, o‘zlarini qanday his qilishlarini so‘raydi; taxminan 40% yoki undan ko‘pi "juda xafa bo‘lardim" deb javob bersa, moslik ehtimoli yuqori.

Bozorga moslikka erishgunga qadar ustuvor vazifa — o‘rganish: foydalanuvchilar bilan har hafta gaplashing va mahsulotni tez o‘zgartiring. Moslikka erishgandan keyin ustuvorlik mijozlarni jalb qilish, operatsiyalar va jamoani kengaytirishga o‘tadi. Moslikdan oldin marketing xarajatlarini oshirish odatda tez ketib qoladigan mijozlarni sotib olishga olib keladi.

Asosiy xulosa: MVP larni oldindan belgilangan muvaffaqiyat mezonlari bilan tajriba sifatida qo‘llang. O‘sishga pul sarflashdan oldin tekislanayotgan saqlab qolish ko‘rsatkichi va mijozlar tomonidan tortilishni izlang.

revenue-models-pricing.title: Daromad modellari va narx belgilash
revenue-models-pricing.summary: Obunalar, tranzaksiyalar, marketpleyslar va foydalanishga asoslangan narxlar hamda narxni qanday tanlash.
revenue-models-pricing.body:
Daromad modeli biznes qiymatni qanday qo‘lga kiritishini tavsiflaydi. Keng tarqalgan modellar: obunalar (dasturiy ta’minot xizmat sifatida modelidagi kabi takroriy oylik yoki yillik to‘lov), tranzaksion sotuvlar (bir martalik xaridlar), marketpleyslar (xaridor va sotuvchilar o‘rtasidagi tranzaksiyalardan komissiya yoki ulush olish), foydalanishga asoslangan narxlar (har bir xabar, gigabayt yoki safar uchun to‘lov), reklama va freemium (foydalanuvchilarning kichik qismini pullik tariflarga o‘tkazadigan bepul daraja).

Marketpleys uchun tushum = umumiy tovar aylanmasi (GMV) × komissiya ulushi. Oyiga 10 milliard so‘mlik buyurtmalarni 15% komissiya bilan qayta ishlaydigan yetkazib berish platformasi 10 milliard emas, 1,5 milliard so‘m tushum oladi. GMV ni tushum bilan chalkashtirish investorlar uchun taqdimotlarda keng tarqalgan xatodir.

Narx belgilashning uchta tayanchi bor. Xarajat ustiga ustama qo‘yish usuli birlik xarajatiga ustama qo‘shadi — bu oddiy, lekin mijoz uchun qiymatni e’tiborsiz qoldiradi. Raqobatchilarga asoslangan narx muqobillarga tenglashadi yoki ulardan arzonroq bo‘ladi. Qiymatga asoslangan narx mijoz oladigan iqtisodiy qiymatdan boshlanadi: agar dasturingiz do‘konga oyiga yo‘qotilgan sotuv va xodimlar vaqti bo‘yicha 2 million so‘m tejasa, 400 000 so‘m narx mijozni aniq yutuqda qoldiradi. Darajali tariflar (asosiy, pro, korporativ) turli mijoz segmentlariga o‘zlari tanlash imkonini beradi va bu qiymat oralig‘ining kattaroq qismini qo‘lga kiritadi.

Asosiy xulosa: mijozlar qiymat oladigan usulga mos daromad modelini tanlang, GMV emas, tushumni ko‘rsating va narxni mijoz qiymatidan kelib chiqib belgilang, xarajatlarni quyi chegara, raqobatchilarni esa mo‘ljal sifatida ishlating.

contribution-margin-breakeven.title: Marjinal daromad va zararsizlik nuqtasi
contribution-margin-breakeven.summary: Har bir sotuv doimiy xarajatlarni qoplashga qancha hissa qo‘shadi va zararsizlikka erishish uchun qancha sotuv kerak.
contribution-margin-breakeven.body:
Birlik boshiga marjinal daromad — narx minus birlik boshiga o‘zgaruvchan xarajat: har bir sotuv doimiy xarajatlarni, so‘ngra foydani qoplashga qo‘shadigan summa. O‘zgaruvchan xarajatlar har bir sotilgan birlik bilan o‘sadi (masalliqlar, qadoqlash, to‘lov komissiyalari, yetkazib berish, sotuv bonuslari); doimiy xarajatlar esa o‘smaydi (ijara, oylik maoshli xodimlar, dasturiy ta’minot obunalari). Marjinal daromad koeffitsienti = marjinal daromad ÷ narx.

Zararsizlik hajmi = doimiy xarajatlar ÷ birlik boshiga marjinal daromad. Misol: tayyor taom to‘plamlari startapi to‘plamlarni 80 000 so‘mdan sotadi. Masalliqlar, qadoqlash, yetkazib berish va to‘lov komissiyalari jami 56 000 so‘m, demak har bir to‘plam 24 000 so‘m (30% marja) qo‘shadi. Oylik doimiy xarajatlar 120 million so‘m bo‘lsa, zararsizlik nuqtasi 120 000 000 ÷ 24 000 = oyiga 5 000 to‘plam. 30 million so‘m maqsadli foyda olish uchun startapga (120 + 30) million ÷ 24 000 = 6 250 to‘plam kerak.

Marjinal daromad o‘sish yordam beradimi yoki zarar keltiradimi, shuni ko‘rsatadi. Agar marja manfiy bo‘lsa, har bir qo‘shimcha sotuv zararni chuqurlashtiradi va miqyos biznesni tuzata olmaydi; chegirmalar, bepul yetkazib berish va subsidiyalangan aksiyalar ko‘pincha buni yashiradi. Birlik iqtisodiyotini yaxshilash narxni oshirish, o‘zgaruvchan xarajatni kamaytirish (yetkazib beruvchilar bilan yaxshiroq shartlar, yetkazib berishda marshrut zichligi, avtomatlashtirish) yoki mahsulot tarkibini yuqori marjali mahsulotlar tomon o‘zgartirishni anglatadi. Operatsion leveraj, ya’ni doimiy xarajatlarning yuqori ulushi zararsizlik nuqtasidan yuqorida foydani tez o‘stiradi, lekin undan pastda zararni keskin oshiradi.

Asosiy xulosa: birlik boshiga marjinal daromad va zararsizlik hajmingizni biling. Marjinal daromadi manfiy bo‘lgan mahsulotni hech qachon kengaytirishga urinmang.

cac-ltv.title: CAC, LTV va o‘zini qoplash muddati
cac-ltv.summary: Mijozlarni jalb qilish qiymat yaratadimi yoki yo‘q qiladimi, shuni ko‘rsatadigan asosiy ko‘rsatkichlar.
cac-ltv.body:
Mijozni jalb qilish xarajati (CAC) — ma’lum davrdagi umumiy sotuv va marketing xarajatlarining jalb qilingan yangi mijozlar soniga nisbati: 50 million so‘m sarflab, 100 ta mijoz jalb qilsangiz, CAC = 500 000 so‘m. Faqat reklamani emas, sotuv xodimlari maoshi va agentlik to‘lovlarini ham kiriting hamda CAC ni kanallar bo‘yicha hisoblang, chunki kanallar bir-biridan juda farq qiladi.

Mijozning umrbod qiymati (LTV) — mijozdan butun munosabatlar davomida kutilayotgan yalpi foyda. Oylik ketish darajasi c bo‘lgan obuna biznesida mijozning o‘rtacha "umri" 1 ÷ c oy, demak LTV = (ARPU × yalpi marja) ÷ ketish darajasi, bu yerda ARPU — foydalanuvchi boshiga oylik o‘rtacha tushum. Misol: ARPU = 100 000 so‘m, yalpi marja = 70% va oylik ketish darajasi = 4%. LTV = 70 000 ÷ 0,04 = 1 750 000 so‘m.

Ikki nisbat o‘sish sog‘lomligini umumlashtiradi. LTV ÷ CAC = 1 750 000 ÷ 500 000 = 3,5; keng tarqalgan mezon — kamida 3, ya’ni jalb qilishga sarflangan har bir so‘m uch so‘m yalpi foyda qaytaradi. CAC ning o‘zini qoplash muddati = CAC ÷ (ARPU × yalpi marja) = 500 000 ÷ 70 000 ≈ 7 oy: jalb qilish xarajatlarini qoplash uchun ketadigan vaqt. Qisqaroq qoplash muddati o‘sishga kamroq pul bog‘lanib qolishini anglatadi, bu esa mablag‘i cheklangan erta bosqichdagi kompaniyalar uchun juda muhim.

Ehtiyot bo‘ling: LTV baholari ketish darajasiga juda sezgir (ketish darajasini ikki baravar kamaytirish LTV ni ikki baravar oshiradi), yosh kompaniyalarda uzoq muddatli saqlab qolish bo‘yicha ma’lumotlar kam, LTV esa tushumdan emas, yalpi foydadan hisoblanishi kerak. Ko‘plab startaplar tushumga asoslangan LTV va qimmat pullik kanallarni yashirgan umumlashtirilgan CAC dan foydalangani uchun qog‘ozda sog‘lom ko‘ringan.

Asosiy xulosa: LTV = ARPU × yalpi marja ÷ ketish darajasi; LTV/CAC kamida 3 bo‘lishiga va o‘zini qoplash muddati taxminan bir yil yoki undan kam bo‘lishiga intiling, bularni kanallar bo‘yicha va ehtiyotkor ketish darajasi bilan hisoblang.

cohorts-retention.title: Kogortalar, mijozlar ketishi va sof tushumni saqlab qolish
cohorts-retention.summary: Biznes haqiqatan yaxshilanayotganini ko‘rish uchun mijozlar guruhlarini vaqt bo‘yicha kuzating.
cohorts-retention.body:
Barcha mijozlar bo‘yicha o‘rtacha ko‘rsatkichlar haqiqiy holatni yashirishi mumkin. Kogorta tahlili mijozlarni qo‘shilgan oyi bo‘yicha guruhlaydi va har bir guruhni vaqt davomida kuzatadi. Saqlab qolish jadvali, masalan, yanvarda qo‘shilgan mijozlarning 0-oyda 100%, 1-oyda 62%, 3-oyda 48% va 6-oyda 45% faol bo‘lganini ko‘rsatadi. Agar keyingi kogortalar avvalgilaridan yaxshiroq saqlanib qolsa, mahsulot yaxshilanmoqda; egri chiziq nolga qarab tushishda davom etsa, biznes marketing xarajatlari to‘ldira olmaydigan "teshik chelak"ka aylangan.

Mijozlar ketishi — davr ichida yo‘qotilgan mijozlar ulushi: ketish darajasi = yo‘qotilgan mijozlar ÷ davr boshidagi mijozlar. 5% oylik ketish darajasi kichik tuyuladi, lekin bu bir yilda mijozlarning taxminan 46% ini yo‘qotishni anglatadi (1 − 0,95¹² ≈ 0,46). Yirik va kichik mijozlar turlicha harakat qilganda tushum bo‘yicha ketish darajasi mijozlar ketishidan farq qilishi mumkin.

Sof tushumni saqlab qolish (NRR) mavjud kogortadan olinadigan tushum, shu jumladan tarifni oshirishlar bilan qanday o‘zgarishini o‘lchaydi: NRR = (boshlang‘ich takroriy tushum + kengayish − qisqarish − ketgan mijozlar tushumi) ÷ boshlang‘ich takroriy tushum. Misol: kogorta yilni 100 million so‘m oylik takroriy tushum bilan boshlaydi, tarifni oshirishlardan 15 million qo‘shadi, tarifni pasaytirishlardan 5 million va bekor qilishlardan 8 million yo‘qotadi. NRR = (100 + 15 − 5 − 8) ÷ 100 = 102%. 100% dan yuqori bo‘lsa, mavjud mijozlar hatto yangi sotuvlarsiz ham tushumni oshiradi — bu eng kuchli obuna bizneslarining belgisidir.

Asosiy xulosa: saqlab qolishni kogortalar bo‘yicha tahlil qiling, oylik ketish darajasining haqiqiy og‘irligini his qilish uchun uni yillik ko‘rsatkichga aylantiring va barqaror o‘sishning eng aniq belgisi sifatida sof tushumni saqlab qolishni kuzating.

growth-channels-funnels.title: O‘sish kanallari va voronkalar
growth-channels-funnels.summary: Mijoz yo‘lini xaritaga tushiring, tor joyni toping va virusli o‘sishni tushuning.
growth-channels-funnels.body:
O‘sish voronkasi mijoz yo‘lini bosqichlarga ajratadi, shunda odamlar qayerda chiqib ketayotganini ko‘rasiz. Ommabop yondashuv — AARRR: jalb qilish (odamlar keladi), faollashtirish (birinchi tajribasi yaxshi bo‘ladi), saqlab qolish (ular qaytib keladi), tavsiya (ular boshqalarni olib keladi) va tushum (ular to‘laydi). Har bir bosqich o‘rtasidagi konversiya darajasini o‘lchang. Misol: 10 000 tashrif buyuruvchi → 1 500 ro‘yxatdan o‘tish (15%) → 600 faollashgan foydalanuvchi (40%) → 240 pullik mijoz (40%). Eng zaif bosqichni yaxshilash odatda eng katta ta’sir beradi; faollashtirishni 40% dan 80% ga oshirish jalb qilishga ko‘proq sarflamasdan pullik mijozlarni ikki baravar oshiradi.

O‘sish kanallariga pullik reklama, qidiruv tizimlari uchun optimallashtirish, kontent, hamkorliklar, to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri sotuvlar, marketpleyslar va ilovalar do‘konlari hamda tavsiya dasturlari kiradi. Dastlab yupqa tarqalib ketish o‘rniga ishlaydigan bir yoki ikki kanalni toping va ularga chuqur e’tibor qarating; har bir kanalning CAC si va kengayish imkoniyati juda farq qiladi. Messenjerlar, ijtimoiy tarmoqlar va mahalliy blogerlar onlayn hayotda ustun bo‘lgan bozorlarda ayniqsa samarali kanal bo‘lishi mumkin.

Virusli o‘sish virusli koeffitsient bilan o‘lchanadi: K = foydalanuvchi boshiga yuborilgan taklifnomalar × taklifnomaning konversiya darajasi. Agar har bir foydalanuvchi 5 kishini taklif qilsa va 10% qo‘shilsa, K = 0,5: har 100 foydalanuvchi yana 50 kishini, keyin 25 kishini va hokazo olib keladi, bu organik o‘sishni 1 ÷ (1 − K) = 2 baravar oshiradi. Faqat K > 1 o‘z-o‘zini ta’minlaydigan eksponensial o‘sishni beradi va bu kamdan-kam uchraydi. Sikl vaqti, ya’ni taklifnomalar qanchalik tez konversiya bo‘lishi K kabi muhim.

Asosiy xulosa: voronkangizni bosqichma-bosqich o‘lchang va avval eng katta tor joyni tuzating, eng yaxshi CAC ga ega kanallarga e’tibor qarating va virusli o‘sishni reja emas, kuchaytirgich sifatida ko‘ring.

burn-runway.title: Pul sarflash sur’ati, pul zaxirasi muddati va pul oqimini rejalashtirish
burn-runway.summary: Kompaniya mavjud pul bilan qancha vaqt yashay oladi va buni hisobga olib qanday rejalashtirish kerak.
burn-runway.body:
Startaplar ko‘pincha mahsulot yaratish va o‘sish davomida yillar davomida zarar ko‘radi, shuning uchun omon qolishni foyda emas, pul belgilaydi. Yalpi sarf (gross burn) — umumiy oylik pul xarajatlari; sof sarf (net burn) — pul xarajatlari minus kelib tushayotgan pul. Pul zaxirasi muddati (runway) = bankdagi pul ÷ sof sarf. Misol: bankda 3,6 milliard so‘m va oylik sof sarf 300 million so‘m bo‘lsa, pul zaxirasi muddati 12 oy.

Investitsiya jalb qilishni pul zaxirasi muddatiga qarab rejalashtiring. Yangi raundni jalb qilish odatda birinchi uchrashuvlardan pul bankka tushguncha bir necha oy davom etadi, shuning uchun ko‘plab asoschilar hali 6–9 oylik pul zaxirasi qolganida boshlaydi. Keyingi bosqichga yetishdan oldin pulning tugashi yomon shartlarga yoki yopilishga majbur qiladi. Foydali savol — kompaniya "sukut bo‘yicha tirikmi": joriy o‘sish sur’atlari va xarajatlarda u pul tugashidan oldin foydaga chiqadimi?

Pul oqimini rejalashtirish oddiy oylik modeldan foydalanadi: boshlang‘ich pul + pul tushumlari − pul chiqimlari = yakuniy pul. Tushum pul bilan bir xil emas: mijozlar kechikib to‘lashi, yillik oldindan to‘lovlar esa pulni oldinroq olib kelishi mumkin. Ssenariylar tuzing (asosiy, ijobiy va salbiy) va tanazzul paytida qanday choralar ko‘rishingizni aniqlang, masalan ishga yollashni to‘xtatish, eng samarasiz marketing kanallarini qisqartirish yoki shartnomalarni qayta muhokama qilish. Xarajatlarni erta qisqartirish faqat ikki oylik pul qolganida qisqartirishdan ancha kam og‘riqli.

Asosiy xulosa: pul zaxirasi muddati = pul ÷ sof sarf. Uni har oy kuzating, kamida olti oy qolganida investitsiya jalb qilishni boshlang va o‘sish kutilganidek bo‘lmasa, qaysi xarajatlarni qisqartirishingizni biling.

fundraising-dilution.title: Investitsiya jalb qilish, baholash va ulush suyultirilishi
fundraising-dilution.summary: Investitsiyagacha va investitsiyadan keyingi baholash, raunddan keyingi egalik ulushi va erta bosqichdagi keng tarqalgan vositalar.
fundraising-dilution.body:
Kapital orqali moliyalashtirish kompaniya ulushining bir qismini investorlarga pul evaziga sotishni anglatadi. Ikkita baholash muhim. Investitsiyagacha baholash (pre-money) — yangi pul kelishidan oldingi kelishilgan qiymat; investitsiyadan keyingi baholash (post-money) = investitsiyagacha baholash + yangi investitsiya. Investorlar ulushi = investitsiya ÷ investitsiyadan keyingi baholash.

Misol: startap 2 million dollarlik investitsiyagacha baholashga kelishib, 500 000 dollar jalb qiladi. Investitsiyadan keyingi baholash 2,5 million dollar, demak investorlar 500 000 ÷ 2 500 000 = 20% ulushga ega bo‘ladi. Avval 100% ga egalik qilgan asoschilar endi 80% ga egalik qiladi. Bu suyultirish: ularning foizi kamayadi, lekin pul kompaniyaga o‘sishda yordam bersa, kattaroq kompaniyaning 80% kichikroq kompaniyaning 100% idan ancha qimmat bo‘lishi mumkin. Investorlar odatda raunddan oldin xodimlar uchun optsionlar fondini (ko‘pincha 10–15%) yaratishni ham talab qiladi, bu asoschilar ulushini yanada suyultiradi.

Bir nechta raund davomida suyultirish to‘planib boradi. Agar asoschilar seed bosqichida 20%, A seriyada 20% va B seriyada 15% dan voz kechsa, ular dastlabki ulushining 0,8 × 0,8 × 0,85 ≈ 54% ini saqlab qoladi. Kapitallashuv jadvali (cap table) har bir raunddan keyin har bir egasining aksiyalarini kuzatib boradi.

Erta raundlarda ko‘pincha narxni belgilashni kechiktiradigan vositalardan foydalaniladi, masalan konvertatsiya qilinadigan qarz yoki SAFE (kelajakdagi kapital bo‘yicha oddiy kelishuv). Ular keyingi narxlangan raundda aksiyalarga aylanadi, odatda erta riskni mukofotlaydigan baholash chegarasi (valuation cap) yoki chegirma bilan. Baholashdan tashqari shartlarni o‘qing: tugatish imtiyozlari, direktorlar kengashidagi o‘rinlar va himoya qoidalari asosiy narxdan ham muhimroq bo‘lishi mumkin. Kapitalga muqobillar: tushumga asoslangan moliyalashtirish, grantlar, bank kreditlari va mijozlardan tushgan tushum hisobiga o‘z kuchi bilan rivojlanish (bootstrapping).

Asosiy xulosa: investitsiyadan keyingi baholash = investitsiyagacha baholash + investitsiya, investor ulushi = investitsiya ÷ investitsiyadan keyingi baholash. Kelajakdagi raundlar bo‘yicha suyultirishni modellashtiring va faqat baholashga emas, shartlarga ham diqqat bilan qarang.

topics.title: Financial Accounting & Valuation
topics.description: Read and connect the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement, understand accrual accounting, analyse performance with ratios, and value a business with discounted cash flows and multiples.

modules.title: The three financial statements
modules.summary: The accounting equation and how the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement fit together.

lessons.title: The accounting equation and double entry
lessons.summary: Assets = liabilities + equity, and why every transaction touches at least two accounts.
lessons.body:
All of financial accounting rests on one identity: Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Assets are resources the business controls that are expected to bring future benefits (cash, receivables, inventory, equipment). Liabilities are obligations to outsiders (supplier bills, loans, taxes owed). Equity is the owners' residual claim: what would be left for owners if all assets were sold at book value and all liabilities paid.

Double-entry bookkeeping keeps the equation in balance by recording every transaction in at least two accounts, with total debits equal to total credits. Example transactions for a new coffee shop: the founder invests 200 million UZS (cash +200, equity +200). The shop borrows 100 million from a bank (cash +100, loans +100). It buys an espresso machine for 120 million in cash (equipment +120, cash −120). It buys coffee beans on credit for 15 million (inventory +15, payables +15). After these transactions, assets are 180 cash + 120 equipment + 15 inventory = 315, and liabilities plus equity are 100 + 15 + 200 = 315.

Revenue increases equity and expenses decrease it, so profit flows into equity through retained earnings. Dividends paid to owners reduce retained earnings. Every financial statement is built from these recorded transactions.

Key takeaway: Assets = Liabilities + Equity always holds. Each transaction changes at least two accounts, and profits accumulate in equity as retained earnings.

lessons.title: The balance sheet
lessons.summary: A snapshot of what a company owns and owes at a point in time.
lessons.body:
The balance sheet shows assets, liabilities and equity at a single date, such as 31 December. It is a snapshot, not a movie. Assets are listed by liquidity. Current assets are expected to turn into cash within a year: cash, accounts receivable (money customers owe), inventory and prepaid expenses. Non-current assets include property, plant and equipment (shown net of accumulated depreciation), intangible assets such as software and licences, and long-term investments.

Liabilities are similarly split. Current liabilities fall due within a year: accounts payable to suppliers, short-term debt, accrued wages and taxes, and deferred revenue (cash received for goods or services not yet delivered). Non-current liabilities include long-term loans, bonds and lease obligations. Equity consists of contributed capital (what owners invested) plus retained earnings (accumulated profits not paid out as dividends).

Example (million UZS): cash 150, receivables 120, inventory 130, equipment (net) 400 give total assets of 800. Payables 90, short-term debt 60, long-term debt 250 and equity 400 give liabilities plus equity of 800. Net working capital is current assets minus current liabilities: (150 + 120 + 130) − (90 + 60) = 250.

Remember that most assets are recorded at historical cost less depreciation, not market value. Valuable internally built assets, such as a strong brand or a skilled team, usually do not appear at all, which is why market value can be far above book value.

Key takeaway: the balance sheet is a point-in-time snapshot ordered by liquidity. Book values are based on historical cost and often differ greatly from market values.

lessons.title: The income statement
lessons.summary: Revenue, expenses and profit over a period, from gross profit down to net income.
lessons.body:
The income statement (profit and loss statement) shows performance over a period, such as a quarter or a year. It starts with revenue and subtracts expenses in layers, each producing a different measure of profit.

Example (million UZS): revenue 1,000. Cost of goods sold, the direct cost of the products sold, is 600, so gross profit is 400 (a 40% gross margin). Operating expenses (salaries, rent, marketing, and depreciation of 40) total 250, giving operating profit, or EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes), of 150, a 15% operating margin. Interest expense of 30 leaves profit before tax of 120. Income tax at 15% is 18, so net income is 102, a net margin of 10.2%.

Analysts often use EBITDA (EBIT plus depreciation and amortization; here 150 + 40 = 190) as a rough proxy for operating cash generation before investment, because depreciation is a non-cash expense. EBITDA ignores the real cost of replacing equipment, so it should never be confused with free cash flow.

Each layer answers a different question. Gross margin shows pricing power and production efficiency. Operating margin shows how well the whole business is run. Net income shows what is left for owners after lenders and the government. Earnings per share (EPS) divides net income by the number of shares.

Key takeaway: revenue − COGS = gross profit; − operating expenses = EBIT; − interest − tax = net income. Compare margins at each level, and remember that profit is not the same as cash.

lessons.title: The cash flow statement
lessons.summary: Operating, investing and financing cash flows, and how to reconcile net income to cash.
lessons.body:
The cash flow statement explains why cash changed during the period. It has three sections. Operating cash flow (CFO) is cash generated by the core business. Investing cash flow covers buying and selling long-term assets; capital expenditure (CapEx) on equipment is the largest item for most firms. Financing cash flow covers borrowing and repaying debt, issuing shares and paying dividends.

Most companies present CFO with the indirect method, starting from net income and adjusting for non-cash items and working capital. Example (million UZS): net income 102, plus depreciation 40 (a non-cash expense), minus an increase in receivables of 30 (sales booked but not yet collected), minus an increase in inventory of 20 (cash spent on stock), plus an increase in payables of 15 (bills not yet paid). CFO = 102 + 40 − 30 − 20 + 15 = 107.

Free cash flow (FCF) is the cash available to all investors after the business has funded its operations and investment: FCF = CFO − CapEx. With CapEx of 80, FCF = 107 − 80 = 27. A profitable, fast-growing company can have negative free cash flow because it is pouring cash into inventory, receivables and equipment, which is why profitable firms can still run out of cash.

The three statements link together: net income from the income statement starts the cash flow statement and flows into retained earnings on the balance sheet, and the net change in cash on the cash flow statement equals the change in the cash line on the balance sheet.

Key takeaway: CFO = net income + non-cash expenses − increases in working capital. FCF = CFO − CapEx, and it is free cash flow, not profit, that pays debts and dividends.

modules.title: Accrual accounting in practice
modules.summary: Revenue recognition, depreciation, inventory costing and working capital.

lessons.title: Revenue recognition and accruals
lessons.summary: Why revenue and expenses are recorded when earned and incurred, not when cash moves.
lessons.body:
Under accrual accounting, revenue is recognized when it is earned, meaning when the company delivers the promised goods or services, and expenses are recognized when they are incurred to generate that revenue (the matching principle). This gives a truer picture of performance than cash accounting, where a large customer payment or supplier bill could make one month look artificially good or bad.

Accruals create balance sheet items that bridge timing differences. Deferred revenue arises when customers pay before delivery. Example: a customer prepays 1.2 million UZS for an annual software subscription in January. On receipt, cash rises by 1.2 million and deferred revenue (a liability) rises by 1.2 million. Each month the company recognizes 100,000 UZS of revenue and reduces deferred revenue by the same amount. Accounts receivable arise in the opposite case, when goods are delivered before payment.

On the expense side, accrued expenses are costs incurred but not yet paid, such as December salaries paid in January; prepaid expenses are payments made in advance, such as a year's insurance, which are expensed month by month. International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS 15) describe a five-step model for revenue: identify the contract, identify the performance obligations, determine the price, allocate it to the obligations and recognize revenue as each obligation is satisfied.

Key takeaway: accrual accounting records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred. Deferred revenue, receivables, accrued and prepaid expenses absorb the timing gaps between profit and cash.

lessons.title: Depreciation and inventory costing
lessons.summary: Spreading the cost of long-lived assets over time, and FIFO versus weighted-average inventory.
lessons.body:
When a company buys equipment that will be used for several years, it does not expense the whole cost at once. It capitalizes the asset on the balance sheet and spreads the cost over its useful life through depreciation, matching cost with the revenue the asset helps generate. Straight-line depreciation = (cost − residual value) ÷ useful life. Example: a delivery van costs 120 million UZS, is expected to last 5 years and to be sold for 20 million at the end. Annual depreciation is (120 − 20) ÷ 5 = 20 million. After two years its net book value is 120 − 40 = 80 million. Accelerated methods, such as declining balance, charge more in early years. Intangible assets such as software are amortized in the same way.

Inventory raises a similar question: which costs go to cost of goods sold and which remain in inventory? Suppose a shop buys 100 units at 10,000 UZS and later 100 units at 12,000 UZS, then sells 150 units. Under FIFO (first in, first out), cost of goods sold is 100 × 10,000 + 50 × 12,000 = 1.6 million, and ending inventory is 50 × 12,000 = 0.6 million. Under weighted-average cost, each unit costs 11,000, so COGS is 1.65 million and ending inventory 0.55 million. When prices are rising, FIFO reports lower COGS and higher profit. (LIFO, last in, first out, is not permitted under IFRS.)

Both choices change reported profit but not the cash the business actually spent, which is why analysts compare cash flow with earnings and read the accounting policy notes.

Key takeaway: depreciation spreads the cost of long-lived assets over their useful lives, and the inventory method decides how costs are split between COGS and inventory. Neither changes cash.

lessons.title: Working capital and the cash conversion cycle
lessons.summary: How long cash is tied up in inventory and receivables before it comes back.
lessons.body:
Net working capital (current assets minus current liabilities) measures the short-term funds tied up in running the business. For operating analysis, focus on the three working capital accounts that move with sales: inventory, receivables and payables.

Each can be expressed in days. Days inventory outstanding (DIO) = inventory ÷ COGS × 365: how long goods sit before being sold. Days sales outstanding (DSO) = receivables ÷ revenue × 365: how long customers take to pay. Days payables outstanding (DPO) = payables ÷ COGS × 365: how long the company takes to pay suppliers. The cash conversion cycle is CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO, the number of days between paying suppliers and collecting from customers.

Example: a distributor holds inventory for 45 days, collects from customers in 30 days and pays suppliers in 25 days. CCC = 45 + 30 − 25 = 50 days. If annual revenue is 3.65 billion UZS (10 million a day), a 50-day cycle ties up roughly 500 million UZS in working capital, and growth increases this need. Cutting DSO by 10 days, through faster invoicing or early-payment discounts, releases about 100 million UZS of cash.

Some businesses have a negative cash conversion cycle: supermarkets and online marketplaces often collect from customers immediately but pay suppliers weeks later, so growth actually generates cash. By contrast, a manufacturer that offers long credit terms can grow itself into a cash crisis.

Key takeaway: CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO. A shorter cycle means less cash tied up in operations, and every day saved releases cash.

modules.title: Financial ratio analysis
modules.summary: Profitability, efficiency, liquidity and solvency ratios, and how to spot low-quality earnings.

lessons.title: Profitability ratios and the DuPont analysis
lessons.summary: Margins, return on assets and return on equity, and what drives them.
lessons.body:
Profitability ratios relate profit to sales or to the capital used. Margins (gross, operating and net) divide each level of profit by revenue. Return on assets, ROA = net income ÷ total assets, shows how much profit the business generates per som of assets. Return on equity, ROE = net income ÷ shareholders' equity, shows the return to owners.

The DuPont analysis splits ROE into three drivers: ROE = (net income ÷ revenue) × (revenue ÷ assets) × (assets ÷ equity), that is, net margin × asset turnover × financial leverage. Using the earlier example (million UZS): net income 102, revenue 1,000, total assets 800 and equity 400. Net margin is 10.2%, asset turnover is 1.25 and leverage (the equity multiplier) is 2.0, so ROE = 10.2% × 1.25 × 2.0 = 25.5%, which matches 102 ÷ 400.

The decomposition shows how a company earns its return. A luxury brand typically has high margins but low turnover; a discount supermarket has thin margins but very high turnover. Two firms with the same ROE can have very different risk: if one achieves it through high leverage, its returns will swing more and it is more exposed to rising interest rates.

Compare ratios with the company's own history and with peers in the same industry, because normal levels vary enormously across sectors.

Key takeaway: ROE = margin × turnover × leverage. Use DuPont analysis to see whether returns come from profitability, efficiency or debt.

lessons.title: Liquidity and solvency ratios
lessons.summary: Can the company pay its bills next month, and can it carry its debt over the long term?
lessons.body:
Liquidity ratios ask whether a company can meet short-term obligations. The current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities; using the balance sheet example (400 ÷ 150), it is about 2.7. The quick ratio excludes inventory, which may be hard to sell quickly: (cash + receivables) ÷ current liabilities = (150 + 120) ÷ 150 = 1.8. A ratio below 1 is a warning sign for most businesses, although firms with fast-turning inventory and negative cash conversion cycles, such as supermarkets, can operate safely below it.

Solvency ratios ask whether the company can carry its debt over the long run. Debt-to-equity = total debt ÷ equity = (60 + 250) ÷ 400 ≈ 0.78. Net debt = debt − cash = 310 − 150 = 160. Net debt ÷ EBITDA = 160 ÷ 190 ≈ 0.8 years, a measure lenders watch closely; many treat levels above 3 to 4 as high for an ordinary company. Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest expense = 150 ÷ 30 = 5 times, meaning operating profit could fall by 80% before it no longer covered interest.

Leverage magnifies results in both directions. Debt is usually cheaper than equity, and interest is tax-deductible, so moderate borrowing can raise ROE. But fixed interest payments must be made in bad years too, and debt in a foreign currency adds exchange-rate risk if revenue is in local currency.

Key takeaway: check liquidity with the current and quick ratios, and solvency with debt-to-equity, net debt/EBITDA and interest coverage. High leverage raises returns in good times and the risk of distress in bad times.

lessons.title: Quality of earnings and red flags
lessons.summary: How to tell whether reported profits are sustainable and backed by cash.
lessons.body:
Two companies can report the same profit with very different quality. High-quality earnings are recurring, come from the core business and are backed by cash. Low-quality earnings rely on one-off gains, aggressive accounting choices or revenue that is never collected.

The first test is to compare operating cash flow with net income over several years. If profits rise steadily while operating cash flow stagnates or falls, ask why. Common red flags include receivables growing much faster than revenue (sales booked to customers who may not pay, or generous credit terms to hit targets), inventory building up faster than sales (possible obsolete stock), frequent changes in accounting policies or depreciation lives, large and recurring “one-off” restructuring charges, and gains from asset sales counted in operating profit.

Be cautious with adjusted metrics such as “adjusted EBITDA”, which exclude items management considers unusual. Some exclusions are reasonable, but recurring costs such as share-based compensation or annual restructuring are real expenses. Read the notes to the financial statements, the auditor's report (a qualified opinion or a change of auditor is a serious warning) and related-party transactions.

A simple accruals ratio helps: (net income − operating cash flow) ÷ average total assets. Persistently high values mean profit is running ahead of cash and have historically predicted weaker future earnings.

Key takeaway: trust profits that are recurring and backed by operating cash flow. Watch receivables, inventory, one-offs, adjusted metrics and the audit report for signs of low-quality earnings.

modules.title: Valuation
modules.summary: The time value of money, discounted cash flow valuation, the cost of capital and valuation multiples.

lessons.title: Time value of money and net present value
lessons.summary: Why a som today is worth more than a som tomorrow, and how to compare cash flows at different dates.
lessons.body:
Money today is worth more than the same amount in the future because it can be invested to earn a return, and because future cash is uncertain and eroded by inflation. Compounding moves money forward: FV = PV × (1 + r)ⁿ. Discounting moves it back: PV = FV ÷ (1 + r)ⁿ, where r is the discount rate per period and n the number of periods.

Example: at a 20% annual discount rate, 100 million UZS received in three years is worth 100 ÷ 1.2³ = 100 ÷ 1.728 ≈ 57.9 million today. The higher the rate or the longer the wait, the lower the present value. Discount rates in local-currency terms must reflect local inflation and interest rates, which is why UZS discount rates are much higher than those used for dollar cash flows.

Net present value (NPV) adds up the present values of all cash flows, including the initial investment: NPV = −C₀ + Σ CFₜ ÷ (1 + r)ᵗ. A project with positive NPV creates value at the chosen discount rate and should be accepted, all else equal. Example: invest 100 million now to receive 50 million at the end of each of the next three years, at r = 20%. PV of inflows = 50/1.2 + 50/1.44 + 50/1.728 ≈ 41.7 + 34.7 + 28.9 = 105.3, so NPV ≈ +5.3 million.

The internal rate of return (IRR) is the discount rate at which NPV equals zero; here it is about 23.4%. IRR is intuitive but can mislead when comparing projects of different sizes or with unusual cash flow patterns, so NPV is the more reliable decision rule.

Key takeaway: PV = FV/(1 + r)ⁿ. Accept projects with positive NPV at a discount rate that reflects their risk and the currency of the cash flows.

lessons.title: Cost of capital: CAPM and WACC
lessons.summary: Estimate the return investors require and combine debt and equity into one discount rate.
lessons.body:
The discount rate for a company's cash flows is the return its investors require, which depends on risk. The cost of equity is commonly estimated with the capital asset pricing model (CAPM): Re = rf + β × (market risk premium). Here rf is the risk-free rate, β (beta) measures how strongly the company's returns move with the overall market, and the market risk premium is the extra return investors demand for holding the market rather than risk-free assets. Example: with rf = 4%, β = 1.2 and a market risk premium of 6%, Re = 4% + 1.2 × 6% = 11.2%.

The cost of debt is the interest rate the company would pay on new borrowing. Because interest is tax-deductible, the after-tax cost of debt is Rd × (1 − t). The weighted average cost of capital combines the two in proportion to their market values: WACC = (E ÷ V) × Re + (D ÷ V) × Rd × (1 − t), where V = E + D.

Example: equity is 70% and debt 30% of the company's value, Rd = 7% and the tax rate is 15%. The after-tax cost of debt is 7% × 0.85 = 5.95%, and WACC = 0.7 × 11.2% + 0.3 × 5.95% ≈ 7.84% + 1.79% = 9.6%.

These example inputs are dollar-based. For cash flows in a currency with higher inflation, such as UZS, the discount rate must be higher to match, and investors in emerging markets usually add a country risk premium. The rule is consistency: discount nominal cash flows at a nominal rate, and use the same currency for both cash flows and discount rate.

Key takeaway: Re = rf + β × market risk premium, and WACC blends the cost of equity and after-tax cost of debt by their market weights. Match the currency and inflation of the discount rate to the cash flows.

lessons.title: Discounted cash flow valuation
lessons.summary: Value a business as the present value of its future free cash flows plus a terminal value.
lessons.body:
A discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation says a business is worth the present value of the free cash flows it will generate. The steps are: forecast free cash flow to the firm (operating profit after tax + depreciation − CapEx − increase in working capital) for an explicit period, usually 5 to 10 years; estimate a terminal value for all cash flows after that; discount everything at the WACC; then subtract net debt to get the value of equity.

The terminal value usually uses the Gordon growth formula: TV = FCFₙ₊₁ ÷ (WACC − g), where g is a long-run growth rate that must be below WACC and should not exceed long-run nominal growth of the economy.

Example (million USD): forecast FCF is 100, 110 and 121 in years 1 to 3, WACC is 12% and long-run growth is 4%. TV at the end of year 3 = 121 × 1.04 ÷ (0.12 − 0.04) = 125.84 ÷ 0.08 ≈ 1,573. Present values: 100 ÷ 1.12 = 89.3; 110 ÷ 1.2544 = 87.7; 121 ÷ 1.4049 = 86.1; and the terminal value 1,573 ÷ 1.4049 ≈ 1,119.6. Enterprise value ≈ 89.3 + 87.7 + 86.1 + 1,119.6 ≈ 1,383. If net debt is 300, equity value ≈ 1,083; with 100 million shares, about 10.8 per share.

Note that the terminal value is about 81% of the total. Small changes to WACC or g move the answer a lot: with g = 5% instead of 4%, TV rises to about 1,815 and enterprise value to roughly 1,555. Always present a sensitivity table across WACC and g, and check that the implied growth and margins are realistic.

Key takeaway: DCF value = PV of forecast free cash flows + PV of terminal value, then subtract net debt for equity value. The result is only as good as the assumptions, so test their sensitivity.

lessons.title: Valuation multiples and comparables
lessons.summary: Value a company quickly by comparing it with similar businesses using EV/EBITDA and P/E.
lessons.body:
Relative valuation prices a company by comparing it with similar companies or recent transactions. It answers “what are investors paying for businesses like this?” rather than building a full forecast, and it is a valuable cross-check on any DCF.

First distinguish two value measures. Equity value (market capitalization) is share price × shares outstanding. Enterprise value (EV) is the value of the whole business to all capital providers: EV = equity value + debt − cash (plus minority interests and preferred stock where relevant). Pair each with a matching metric: EV with measures before interest such as EBITDA, EBIT or revenue; equity value with measures after interest such as net income.

Common multiples are EV/EBITDA, EV/revenue (used for unprofitable, fast-growing firms) and the price-to-earnings ratio, P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Example: comparable companies trade at a median EV/EBITDA of 8x. Our company has EBITDA of 190 million, so its implied EV = 8 × 190 = 1,520 million. Subtracting net debt of 160 million gives an equity value of 1,360 million; with 100 million shares, about 13.6 per share.

Multiples embed assumptions about growth, risk and returns on capital, so choose peers that really are similar in industry, size, growth, margins and market, and adjust for differences. A company growing twice as fast as its peers deserves a higher multiple. Watch for one-off items that distort EBITDA or earnings, and remember that multiples from another country or a booming market may not transfer.

Key takeaway: EV = equity value + net debt. Use EV multiples with pre-interest metrics and equity multiples with post-interest metrics, choose genuinely comparable peers, and cross-check against a DCF.

accounting-equation.title: Buxgalteriya tenglamasi va ikki yoqlama yozuv
accounting-equation.summary: Aktivlar = majburiyatlar + kapital va nima uchun har bir operatsiya kamida ikkita hisobvaraqqa ta’sir qiladi.
accounting-equation.body:
Butun moliyaviy hisob bitta ayniyatga asoslanadi: Aktivlar = Majburiyatlar + Kapital. Aktivlar — biznes nazorat qiladigan va kelajakda foyda keltirishi kutilayotgan resurslar (pul mablag‘lari, debitorlik qarzlari, tovar-moddiy zaxiralar, uskunalar). Majburiyatlar — tashqi tomonlar oldidagi majburiyatlar (yetkazib beruvchilar hisob-fakturalari, kreditlar, to‘lanishi kerak bo‘lgan soliqlar). Kapital — egalarning qoldiq huquqi: barcha aktivlar balans qiymatida sotilib, barcha majburiyatlar to‘langanda egalar uchun qoladigan summa.

Ikki yoqlama yozuv tenglamani muvozanatda ushlab turadi: har bir operatsiya kamida ikkita hisobvaraqda qayd etiladi va jami debet jami kreditga teng bo‘ladi. Yangi qahvaxona uchun misol operatsiyalar: asoschi 200 million so‘m kiritadi (pul +200, kapital +200). Qahvaxona bankdan 100 million qarz oladi (pul +100, kreditlar +100). U 120 million so‘mga naqd pulga espresso apparati sotib oladi (uskunalar +120, pul −120). U 15 millionlik qahva donini nasiyaga sotib oladi (zaxiralar +15, kreditorlik qarzlari +15). Bu operatsiyalardan keyin aktivlar 180 pul + 120 uskunalar + 15 zaxiralar = 315 ga, majburiyatlar va kapital esa 100 + 15 + 200 = 315 ga teng.

Tushum kapitalni oshiradi, xarajatlar esa kamaytiradi, shuning uchun foyda taqsimlanmagan foyda orqali kapitalga o‘tadi. Egalarga to‘langan dividendlar taqsimlanmagan foydani kamaytiradi. Har bir moliyaviy hisobot ana shu qayd etilgan operatsiyalardan tuziladi.

Asosiy xulosa: Aktivlar = Majburiyatlar + Kapital tenglamasi har doim bajariladi. Har bir operatsiya kamida ikkita hisobvaraqni o‘zgartiradi, foyda esa kapitalda taqsimlanmagan foyda sifatida to‘planadi.

balance-sheet.title: Buxgalteriya balansi
balance-sheet.summary: Kompaniyaning ma’lum bir sanadagi mulki va qarzlarining surati.
balance-sheet.body:
Balans aktivlar, majburiyatlar va kapitalni bitta sanada, masalan 31 dekabr holatiga ko‘rsatadi. Bu film emas, suratdir. Aktivlar likvidlik bo‘yicha tartiblanadi. Joriy aktivlar bir yil ichida pulga aylanishi kutiladi: pul mablag‘lari, debitorlik qarzlari (mijozlarning qarzi), tovar-moddiy zaxiralar va oldindan to‘langan xarajatlar. Uzoq muddatli aktivlarga asosiy vositalar (to‘plangan amortizatsiya chegirilgan holda), dasturiy ta’minot va litsenziyalar kabi nomoddiy aktivlar hamda uzoq muddatli investitsiyalar kiradi.

Majburiyatlar ham xuddi shunday bo‘linadi. Joriy majburiyatlar bir yil ichida to‘lanishi kerak: yetkazib beruvchilarga kreditorlik qarzlari, qisqa muddatli kreditlar, hisoblangan ish haqi va soliqlar hamda kechiktirilgan daromad (hali yetkazib berilmagan tovar yoki xizmatlar uchun olingan pul). Uzoq muddatli majburiyatlarga uzoq muddatli kreditlar, obligatsiyalar va ijara majburiyatlari kiradi. Kapital ustav kapitali (egalar kiritgan mablag‘) va taqsimlanmagan foydadan (dividend sifatida to‘lanmagan to‘plangan foyda) iborat.

Misol (million so‘m): pul 150, debitorlik qarzlari 120, zaxiralar 130, uskunalar (sof) 400 — jami aktivlar 800. Kreditorlik qarzlari 90, qisqa muddatli kredit 60, uzoq muddatli kredit 250 va kapital 400 — majburiyatlar va kapital jami 800. Sof aylanma kapital — joriy aktivlar minus joriy majburiyatlar: (150 + 120 + 130) − (90 + 60) = 250.

Yodda tuting: aktivlarning aksariyati bozor qiymatida emas, balki tarixiy qiymatdan amortizatsiya chegirilgan holda qayd etiladi. Kuchli brend yoki malakali jamoa kabi ichki yaratilgan qimmatli aktivlar odatda umuman ko‘rinmaydi, shuning uchun bozor qiymati balans qiymatidan ancha yuqori bo‘lishi mumkin.

Asosiy xulosa: balans — likvidlik bo‘yicha tartiblangan ma’lum sanadagi surat. Balans qiymatlari tarixiy qiymatga asoslanadi va ko‘pincha bozor qiymatidan juda farq qiladi.

income-statement.title: Moliyaviy natijalar to‘g‘risidagi hisobot
income-statement.summary: Davr davomidagi tushum, xarajatlar va foyda: yalpi foydadan sof foydagacha.
income-statement.body:
Moliyaviy natijalar to‘g‘risidagi hisobot (foyda va zararlar hisoboti) chorak yoki yil kabi davr davomidagi faoliyat natijalarini ko‘rsatadi. U tushumdan boshlanadi va xarajatlarni qatlamma-qatlam ayiradi, har bir qatlam foydaning turli o‘lchovini beradi.

Misol (million so‘m): tushum 1 000. Sotilgan mahsulot tannarxi, ya’ni sotilgan mahsulotlarning bevosita xarajati 600, demak yalpi foyda 400 (40% yalpi marja). Operatsion xarajatlar (ish haqi, ijara, marketing va 40 miqdoridagi amortizatsiya) jami 250, bu esa 150 operatsion foyda yoki EBIT (foiz va soliqlargacha bo‘lgan foyda) ni beradi, ya’ni 15% operatsion marja. 30 foiz xarajatidan keyin soliqqa tortilgunga qadar foyda 120 qoladi. 15% stavkadagi foyda solig‘i 18 ga teng, demak sof foyda 102, sof marja esa 10,2%.

Tahlilchilar ko‘pincha EBITDA dan (EBIT plyus amortizatsiya; bu yerda 150 + 40 = 190) investitsiyalargacha operatsion pul yaratishning taxminiy ko‘rsatkichi sifatida foydalanadi, chunki amortizatsiya pulsiz xarajat. EBITDA uskunalarni almashtirishning haqiqiy xarajatini e’tiborsiz qoldiradi, shuning uchun uni hech qachon erkin pul oqimi bilan chalkashtirmaslik kerak.

Har bir qatlam turli savolga javob beradi. Yalpi marja narx belgilash qudrati va ishlab chiqarish samaradorligini ko‘rsatadi. Operatsion marja butun biznes qanchalik yaxshi boshqarilishini ko‘rsatadi. Sof foyda kreditorlar va davlatdan keyin egalarga nima qolishini ko‘rsatadi. Bir aksiyaga to‘g‘ri keladigan foyda (EPS) sof foydani aksiyalar soniga bo‘ladi.

Asosiy xulosa: tushum − tannarx = yalpi foyda; − operatsion xarajatlar = EBIT; − foizlar − soliq = sof foyda. Har bir darajadagi marjalarni solishtiring va foyda pul bilan bir xil emasligini yodda tuting.

cash-flow-statement.title: Pul oqimlari to‘g‘risidagi hisobot
cash-flow-statement.summary: Operatsion, investitsion va moliyaviy pul oqimlari hamda sof foydani pul bilan qanday solishtirish.
cash-flow-statement.body:
Pul oqimlari to‘g‘risidagi hisobot davr davomida pul mablag‘lari nima uchun o‘zgarganini tushuntiradi. U uch bo‘limdan iborat. Operatsion pul oqimi (CFO) — asosiy biznes yaratgan pul. Investitsion pul oqimi uzoq muddatli aktivlarni sotib olish va sotishni qamrab oladi; ko‘pchilik firmalar uchun eng katta modda uskunalarga kapital xarajatlar (CapEx). Moliyaviy pul oqimi qarz olish va uni qaytarish, aksiyalar chiqarish va dividendlar to‘lashni qamrab oladi.

Ko‘pchilik kompaniyalar CFO ni bilvosita usulda taqdim etadi: sof foydadan boshlab, pulsiz moddalar va aylanma kapital bo‘yicha tuzatishlar kiritiladi. Misol (million so‘m): sof foyda 102, plyus amortizatsiya 40 (pulsiz xarajat), minus debitorlik qarzlarining 30 ga oshishi (qayd etilgan, lekin hali undirilmagan sotuvlar), minus zaxiralarning 20 ga oshishi (zaxiraga sarflangan pul), plyus kreditorlik qarzlarining 15 ga oshishi (hali to‘lanmagan hisoblar). CFO = 102 + 40 − 30 − 20 + 15 = 107.

Erkin pul oqimi (FCF) — biznes o‘z operatsiyalari va investitsiyalarini moliyalashtirgandan keyin barcha investorlar uchun mavjud bo‘lgan pul: FCF = CFO − CapEx. CapEx 80 bo‘lsa, FCF = 107 − 80 = 27. Foydali, tez o‘sayotgan kompaniya manfiy erkin pul oqimiga ega bo‘lishi mumkin, chunki u zaxiralar, debitorlik qarzlari va uskunalarga pul quymoqda — shuning uchun foydali firmalar ham pulsiz qolishi mumkin.

Uchta hisobot bir-biriga bog‘langan: moliyaviy natijalar hisobotidagi sof foyda pul oqimlari hisobotini boshlaydi va balansdagi taqsimlanmagan foydaga o‘tadi, pul oqimlari hisobotidagi pulning sof o‘zgarishi esa balansdagi pul mablag‘lari qatorining o‘zgarishiga teng.

Asosiy xulosa: CFO = sof foyda + pulsiz xarajatlar − aylanma kapitalning oshishi. FCF = CFO − CapEx va qarzlar hamda dividendlarni foyda emas, erkin pul oqimi to‘laydi.

revenue-recognition-accruals.title: Tushumni tan olish va hisoblangan moddalar
revenue-recognition-accruals.summary: Nima uchun tushum va xarajatlar pul harakatlanganda emas, balki ishlab topilganda va yuzaga kelganda qayd etiladi.
revenue-recognition-accruals.body:
Hisoblash usulida tushum ishlab topilganda, ya’ni kompaniya va’da qilingan tovar yoki xizmatlarni yetkazib berganda tan olinadi, xarajatlar esa shu tushumni yaratish uchun yuzaga kelganda tan olinadi (moslik tamoyili). Bu kassa usuliga qaraganda faoliyat haqida haqqoniyroq tasavvur beradi, chunki kassa usulida yirik mijoz to‘lovi yoki yetkazib beruvchi hisobi bir oyni sun’iy ravishda yaxshi yoki yomon ko‘rsatishi mumkin.

Hisoblangan moddalar vaqt farqlarini bog‘laydigan balans moddalarini yaratadi. Kechiktirilgan daromad mijozlar yetkazib berishdan oldin to‘laganda yuzaga keladi. Misol: mijoz yanvarda yillik dasturiy ta’minot obunasi uchun 1,2 million so‘m oldindan to‘laydi. To‘lov olinganda pul 1,2 millionga, kechiktirilgan daromad (majburiyat) ham 1,2 millionga oshadi. Har oy kompaniya 100 000 so‘m tushumni tan oladi va kechiktirilgan daromadni shuncha miqdorga kamaytiradi. Debitorlik qarzlari teskari holatda, ya’ni tovarlar to‘lovdan oldin yetkazib berilganda yuzaga keladi.

Xarajatlar tomonida hisoblangan xarajatlar — yuzaga kelgan, lekin hali to‘lanmagan xarajatlar, masalan yanvarda to‘lanadigan dekabr ish haqi; oldindan to‘langan xarajatlar — bir yillik sug‘urta kabi oldindan qilingan to‘lovlar bo‘lib, ular oyma-oy xarajatga o‘tkaziladi. Moliyaviy hisobotning xalqaro standartlari (MHXS 15) tushum uchun besh bosqichli modelni tavsiflaydi: shartnomani aniqlash, bajariladigan majburiyatlarni aniqlash, narxni belgilash, uni majburiyatlarga taqsimlash va har bir majburiyat bajarilganda tushumni tan olish.

Asosiy xulosa: hisoblash usuli tushumni ishlab topilganda, xarajatlarni esa yuzaga kelganda qayd etadi. Kechiktirilgan daromad, debitorlik qarzlari, hisoblangan va oldindan to‘langan xarajatlar foyda va pul o‘rtasidagi vaqt farqlarini o‘ziga oladi.

depreciation-inventory.title: Amortizatsiya va zaxiralarni baholash
depreciation-inventory.summary: Uzoq muddatli aktivlar qiymatini vaqt bo‘yicha taqsimlash hamda FIFO va o‘rtacha tortilgan qiymat usullari.
depreciation-inventory.body:
Kompaniya bir necha yil foydalaniladigan uskunani sotib olganda, butun qiymatni birdaniga xarajatga o‘tkazmaydi. U aktivni balansda kapitallashtiradi va qiymatini amortizatsiya orqali foydali xizmat muddatiga taqsimlaydi, shu bilan xarajatni aktiv yaratishga yordam beradigan tushum bilan moslashtiradi. To‘g‘ri chiziqli amortizatsiya = (boshlang‘ich qiymat − tugatish qiymati) ÷ foydali xizmat muddati. Misol: yetkazib berish furgoni 120 million so‘m turadi, 5 yil xizmat qilishi va oxirida 20 millionga sotilishi kutiladi. Yillik amortizatsiya (120 − 20) ÷ 5 = 20 million. Ikki yildan keyin uning sof balans qiymati 120 − 40 = 80 million. Kamayib boruvchi qoldiq kabi tezlashtirilgan usullar dastlabki yillarda ko‘proq amortizatsiya hisoblaydi. Dasturiy ta’minot kabi nomoddiy aktivlar ham xuddi shunday amortizatsiya qilinadi.

Zaxiralar ham shunga o‘xshash savol tug‘diradi: qaysi xarajatlar sotilgan mahsulot tannarxiga o‘tadi va qaysilari zaxirada qoladi? Faraz qilaylik, do‘kon 100 birlikni 10 000 so‘mdan, keyinroq yana 100 birlikni 12 000 so‘mdan sotib oladi, so‘ng 150 birlik sotadi. FIFO (birinchi kirgan — birinchi chiqadi) usulida tannarx 100 × 10 000 + 50 × 12 000 = 1,6 million, yakuniy zaxira esa 50 × 12 000 = 0,6 million. O‘rtacha tortilgan qiymat usulida har bir birlik 11 000 turadi, demak tannarx 1,65 million, yakuniy zaxira 0,55 million. Narxlar oshayotganda FIFO pastroq tannarx va yuqoriroq foyda ko‘rsatadi. (LIFO, ya’ni oxirgi kirgan — birinchi chiqadi usuli MHXS bo‘yicha ruxsat etilmaydi.)

Ikkala tanlov ham hisobotdagi foydani o‘zgartiradi, lekin biznes haqiqatda sarflagan pulni o‘zgartirmaydi, shuning uchun tahlilchilar pul oqimini foyda bilan solishtiradi va hisob siyosati izohlarini o‘qiydi.

Asosiy xulosa: amortizatsiya uzoq muddatli aktivlar qiymatini ularning foydali xizmat muddatiga taqsimlaydi, zaxiralarni baholash usuli esa xarajatlar tannarx va zaxira o‘rtasida qanday bo‘linishini belgilaydi. Ularning hech biri pulni o‘zgartirmaydi.

working-capital.title: Aylanma kapital va pul aylanish sikli
working-capital.summary: Pul qaytib kelgunga qadar zaxiralar va debitorlik qarzlarida qancha vaqt band bo‘lib turadi.
working-capital.body:
Sof aylanma kapital (joriy aktivlar minus joriy majburiyatlar) biznesni yuritishga band bo‘lgan qisqa muddatli mablag‘larni o‘lchaydi. Operatsion tahlil uchun sotuv bilan birga o‘zgaradigan uchta aylanma kapital hisobvarag‘iga e’tibor qarating: zaxiralar, debitorlik va kreditorlik qarzlari.

Ularning har birini kunlarda ifodalash mumkin. Zaxiralar aylanish davri (DIO) = zaxiralar ÷ tannarx × 365: tovarlar sotilgunga qadar qancha turadi. Debitorlik qarzlari aylanish davri (DSO) = debitorlik qarzlari ÷ tushum × 365: mijozlar to‘lash uchun qancha vaqt oladi. Kreditorlik qarzlari aylanish davri (DPO) = kreditorlik qarzlari ÷ tannarx × 365: kompaniya yetkazib beruvchilarga to‘lash uchun qancha vaqt oladi. Pul aylanish sikli CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO, ya’ni yetkazib beruvchilarga to‘lash va mijozlardan pul undirish o‘rtasidagi kunlar soni.

Misol: distribyutor zaxiralarni 45 kun saqlaydi, mijozlardan 30 kunda pul undiradi va yetkazib beruvchilarga 25 kunda to‘laydi. CCC = 45 + 30 − 25 = 50 kun. Agar yillik tushum 3,65 milliard so‘m (kuniga 10 million) bo‘lsa, 50 kunlik sikl aylanma kapitalda taxminan 500 million so‘mni band qiladi va o‘sish bu ehtiyojni oshiradi. Tezroq hisob-faktura yuborish yoki erta to‘lov chegirmalari orqali DSO ni 10 kunga qisqartirish taxminan 100 million so‘m pulni bo‘shatadi.

Ba’zi bizneslarda pul aylanish sikli manfiy bo‘ladi: supermarketlar va onlayn marketpleyslar ko‘pincha mijozlardan pulni darhol oladi, yetkazib beruvchilarga esa haftalar o‘tib to‘laydi, shuning uchun o‘sish aslida pul yaratadi. Aksincha, uzoq kredit muddatlarini taklif qiladigan ishlab chiqaruvchi o‘sish natijasida pul inqiroziga tushib qolishi mumkin.

Asosiy xulosa: CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO. Qisqaroq sikl operatsiyalarda kamroq pul band bo‘lishini anglatadi va tejalgan har bir kun pulni bo‘shatadi.

profitability-dupont.title: Rentabellik koeffitsientlari va DuPont tahlili
profitability-dupont.summary: Marjalar, aktivlar rentabelligi va kapital rentabelligi hamda ularni nima harakatlantiradi.
profitability-dupont.body:
Rentabellik koeffitsientlari foydani sotuvga yoki foydalanilgan kapitalga nisbatlaydi. Marjalar (yalpi, operatsion va sof) foydaning har bir darajasini tushumga bo‘ladi. Aktivlar rentabelligi, ROA = sof foyda ÷ jami aktivlar, biznes aktivlarning har bir so‘miga qancha foyda yaratishini ko‘rsatadi. Kapital rentabelligi, ROE = sof foyda ÷ aksiyadorlar kapitali, egalarga qaytimni ko‘rsatadi.

DuPont tahlili ROE ni uchta omilga ajratadi: ROE = (sof foyda ÷ tushum) × (tushum ÷ aktivlar) × (aktivlar ÷ kapital), ya’ni sof marja × aktivlar aylanuvchanligi × moliyaviy leveraj. Avvalgi misoldan foydalanamiz (million so‘m): sof foyda 102, tushum 1 000, jami aktivlar 800 va kapital 400. Sof marja 10,2%, aktivlar aylanuvchanligi 1,25 va leveraj (kapital multiplikatori) 2,0, demak ROE = 10,2% × 1,25 × 2,0 = 25,5%, bu 102 ÷ 400 ga mos keladi.

Bu ajratish kompaniya o‘z daromadini qanday topishini ko‘rsatadi. Hashamatli brend odatda yuqori marjaga, lekin past aylanuvchanlikka ega; arzon narxli supermarket esa yupqa marjaga, lekin juda yuqori aylanuvchanlikka ega. Bir xil ROE ga ega ikki firma juda turli riskka ega bo‘lishi mumkin: agar biri unga yuqori leveraj orqali erishsa, uning daromadlari ko‘proq tebranadi va u foiz stavkalari oshishiga ko‘proq duch keladi.

Koeffitsientlarni kompaniyaning o‘z tarixi va bir tarmoqdagi raqobatchilar bilan solishtiring, chunki odatiy darajalar sohalar bo‘yicha juda katta farq qiladi.

Asosiy xulosa: ROE = marja × aylanuvchanlik × leveraj. Daromad rentabellik, samaradorlik yoki qarzdan kelayotganini ko‘rish uchun DuPont tahlilidan foydalaning.

liquidity-solvency.title: Likvidlik va to‘lov qobiliyati koeffitsientlari
liquidity-solvency.summary: Kompaniya keyingi oy hisoblarini to‘lay oladimi va uzoq muddatda qarzini ko‘tara oladimi?
liquidity-solvency.body:
Likvidlik koeffitsientlari kompaniya qisqa muddatli majburiyatlarini bajara oladimi, degan savolga javob beradi. Joriy likvidlik koeffitsienti = joriy aktivlar ÷ joriy majburiyatlar; balans misolidan foydalansak (400 ÷ 150), u taxminan 2,7 ga teng. Tez likvidlik koeffitsienti tez sotish qiyin bo‘lishi mumkin bo‘lgan zaxiralarni chiqarib tashlaydi: (pul + debitorlik qarzlari) ÷ joriy majburiyatlar = (150 + 120) ÷ 150 = 1,8. Ko‘pchilik bizneslar uchun 1 dan past koeffitsient ogohlantiruvchi belgi, garchi supermarketlar kabi zaxiralari tez aylanadigan va pul aylanish sikli manfiy bo‘lgan firmalar undan pastda ham xavfsiz ishlay olsa ham.

To‘lov qobiliyati koeffitsientlari kompaniya uzoq muddatda qarzini ko‘tara oladimi, degan savolga javob beradi. Qarzning kapitalga nisbati = jami qarz ÷ kapital = (60 + 250) ÷ 400 ≈ 0,78. Sof qarz = qarz − pul = 310 − 150 = 160. Sof qarz ÷ EBITDA = 160 ÷ 190 ≈ 0,8 yil — kreditorlar diqqat bilan kuzatadigan ko‘rsatkich; ko‘pchilik oddiy kompaniya uchun 3–4 dan yuqori darajalarni yuqori deb hisoblaydi. Foizlarni qoplash koeffitsienti = EBIT ÷ foiz xarajatlari = 150 ÷ 30 = 5 marta, ya’ni operatsion foyda foizlarni qoplay olmay qolishidan oldin 80% ga tushishi mumkin.

Leveraj natijalarni ikkala yo‘nalishda ham kuchaytiradi. Qarz odatda kapitaldan arzonroq va foizlar soliqqa tortiladigan bazadan chegiriladi, shuning uchun mo‘tadil qarz olish ROE ni oshirishi mumkin. Ammo qat’iy foiz to‘lovlari yomon yillarda ham to‘lanishi kerak, xorijiy valyutadagi qarz esa tushum milliy valyutada bo‘lsa, valyuta kursi riskini qo‘shadi.

Asosiy xulosa: likvidlikni joriy va tez likvidlik koeffitsientlari bilan, to‘lov qobiliyatini esa qarzning kapitalga nisbati, sof qarz/EBITDA va foizlarni qoplash koeffitsienti bilan tekshiring. Yuqori leveraj yaxshi davrlarda daromadni, yomon davrlarda esa inqiroz riskini oshiradi.

earnings-quality.title: Foyda sifati va xavf belgilari
earnings-quality.summary: Hisobotdagi foyda barqaror va pul bilan ta’minlanganligini qanday aniqlash mumkin.
earnings-quality.body:
Ikki kompaniya bir xil foydani juda turli sifat bilan ko‘rsatishi mumkin. Yuqori sifatli foyda takrorlanuvchi, asosiy biznesdan keladi va pul bilan ta’minlangan. Past sifatli foyda bir martalik daromadlar, agressiv hisob tanlovlari yoki hech qachon undirilmaydigan tushumga tayanadi.

Birinchi test — bir necha yil davomida operatsion pul oqimini sof foyda bilan solishtirish. Agar foyda barqaror o‘sib, operatsion pul oqimi turg‘un qolsa yoki kamaysa, sababini so‘rang. Keng tarqalgan xavf belgilari: debitorlik qarzlarining tushumdan ancha tez o‘sishi (to‘lamasligi mumkin bo‘lgan mijozlarga qayd etilgan sotuvlar yoki rejalarni bajarish uchun saxiy kredit shartlari), zaxiralarning sotuvdan tezroq to‘planishi (eskirgan zaxira ehtimoli), hisob siyosati yoki amortizatsiya muddatlarining tez-tez o‘zgarishi, katta va takrorlanuvchi "bir martalik" qayta tuzish xarajatlari hamda aktivlarni sotishdan olingan daromadlarning operatsion foydaga kiritilishi.

"Tuzatilgan EBITDA" kabi tuzatilgan ko‘rsatkichlarga ehtiyotkorlik bilan yondashing, ular rahbariyat g‘ayrioddiy deb hisoblagan moddalarni chiqarib tashlaydi. Ba’zi istisnolar asosli, lekin aksiyalar bilan rag‘batlantirish yoki har yilgi qayta tuzish kabi takrorlanuvchi xarajatlar haqiqiy xarajatlardir. Moliyaviy hisobotlarga izohlarni, auditor xulosasini (shartli xulosa yoki auditorning almashtirilishi jiddiy ogohlantirishdir) va aloqador tomonlar bilan operatsiyalarni o‘qing.

Oddiy hisoblangan moddalar koeffitsienti yordam beradi: (sof foyda − operatsion pul oqimi) ÷ jami aktivlarning o‘rtacha qiymati. Doimiy yuqori qiymatlar foyda puldan oldinda ketayotganini anglatadi va tarixan kelajakda zaifroq foydani bashorat qilgan.

Asosiy xulosa: takrorlanuvchi va operatsion pul oqimi bilan ta’minlangan foydaga ishoning. Past sifatli foyda belgilarini aniqlash uchun debitorlik qarzlari, zaxiralar, bir martalik moddalar, tuzatilgan ko‘rsatkichlar va auditor xulosasini kuzating.

time-value-of-money.title: Pulning vaqt qiymati va sof joriy qiymat
time-value-of-money.summary: Nima uchun bugungi so‘m ertangi so‘mdan qimmatroq va turli sanalardagi pul oqimlarini qanday solishtirish mumkin.
time-value-of-money.body:
Bugungi pul kelajakdagi xuddi shu summadan qimmatroq, chunki uni daromad olish uchun investitsiya qilish mumkin, kelajakdagi pul esa noaniq va inflyatsiya tomonidan qadrsizlanadi. Murakkab foiz pulni oldinga suradi: FV = PV × (1 + r)ⁿ. Diskontlash uni orqaga qaytaradi: PV = FV ÷ (1 + r)ⁿ, bu yerda r — bir davr uchun diskont stavkasi, n — davrlar soni.

Misol: yillik 20% diskont stavkasida uch yildan keyin olinadigan 100 million so‘m bugun 100 ÷ 1,2³ = 100 ÷ 1,728 ≈ 57,9 million turadi. Stavka qanchalik yuqori yoki kutish qanchalik uzoq bo‘lsa, joriy qiymat shunchalik past bo‘ladi. Milliy valyutadagi diskont stavkalari mahalliy inflyatsiya va foiz stavkalarini aks ettirishi kerak, shuning uchun so‘mdagi diskont stavkalari dollardagi pul oqimlari uchun ishlatiladiganlardan ancha yuqori.

Sof joriy qiymat (NPV) barcha pul oqimlarining, shu jumladan dastlabki investitsiyaning joriy qiymatlarini qo‘shadi: NPV = −C₀ + Σ CFₜ ÷ (1 + r)ᵗ. Musbat NPV ga ega loyiha tanlangan diskont stavkasida qiymat yaratadi va boshqa sharoitlar teng bo‘lganda qabul qilinishi kerak. Misol: hozir 100 million investitsiya qilib, keyingi uch yilning har biri oxirida 50 million olish, r = 20%. Tushumlarning joriy qiymati = 50/1,2 + 50/1,44 + 50/1,728 ≈ 41,7 + 34,7 + 28,9 = 105,3, demak NPV ≈ +5,3 million.

Ichki daromadlilik me’yori (IRR) — NPV nolga teng bo‘ladigan diskont stavkasi; bu yerda u taxminan 23,4%. IRR tushunarli, lekin turli hajmdagi yoki g‘ayrioddiy pul oqimlariga ega loyihalarni solishtirishda chalg‘itishi mumkin, shuning uchun NPV ishonchliroq qaror qoidasidir.

Asosiy xulosa: PV = FV/(1 + r)ⁿ. Loyihalarni ularning riski va pul oqimlari valyutasini aks ettiruvchi diskont stavkasida NPV musbat bo‘lsa qabul qiling.

cost-of-capital.title: Kapital qiymati: CAPM va WACC
cost-of-capital.summary: Investorlar talab qiladigan daromadni baholang va qarz hamda kapitalni bitta diskont stavkasiga birlashtiring.
cost-of-capital.body:
Kompaniya pul oqimlari uchun diskont stavkasi uning investorlari talab qiladigan daromad bo‘lib, u riskka bog‘liq. Kapital qiymati odatda kapital aktivlarini baholash modeli (CAPM) bilan baholanadi: Re = rf + β × (bozor risk mukofoti). Bu yerda rf — risksiz stavka, β (beta) kompaniya daromadlari umumiy bozor bilan qanchalik kuchli birga harakatlanishini o‘lchaydi, bozor risk mukofoti esa investorlar risksiz aktivlar o‘rniga bozorni ushlab turish uchun talab qiladigan qo‘shimcha daromad. Misol: rf = 4%, β = 1,2 va bozor risk mukofoti 6% bo‘lsa, Re = 4% + 1,2 × 6% = 11,2%.

Qarz qiymati — kompaniya yangi qarz bo‘yicha to‘laydigan foiz stavkasi. Foizlar soliqqa tortiladigan bazadan chegirilgani uchun qarzning soliqdan keyingi qiymati Rd × (1 − t) ga teng. Kapitalning o‘rtacha tortilgan qiymati ikkalasini ularning bozor qiymatlariga mutanosib ravishda birlashtiradi: WACC = (E ÷ V) × Re + (D ÷ V) × Rd × (1 − t), bu yerda V = E + D.

Misol: kompaniya qiymatining 70% ini kapital va 30% ini qarz tashkil etadi, Rd = 7% va soliq stavkasi 15%. Qarzning soliqdan keyingi qiymati 7% × 0,85 = 5,95%, WACC esa = 0,7 × 11,2% + 0,3 × 5,95% ≈ 7,84% + 1,79% = 9,6%.

Bu misoldagi ma’lumotlar dollarga asoslangan. So‘m kabi inflyatsiyasi yuqoriroq valyutadagi pul oqimlari uchun diskont stavkasi ham mos ravishda yuqoriroq bo‘lishi kerak, rivojlanayotgan bozorlardagi investorlar esa odatda mamlakat risk mukofotini qo‘shadi. Qoida — izchillik: nominal pul oqimlarini nominal stavkada diskontlang va pul oqimlari hamda diskont stavkasi uchun bir xil valyutadan foydalaning.

Asosiy xulosa: Re = rf + β × bozor risk mukofoti, WACC esa kapital qiymati va qarzning soliqdan keyingi qiymatini ularning bozor ulushlari bo‘yicha birlashtiradi. Diskont stavkasining valyutasi va inflyatsiyasini pul oqimlariga moslang.

dcf-valuation.title: Diskontlangan pul oqimlari asosida baholash
dcf-valuation.summary: Biznesni uning kelajakdagi erkin pul oqimlari va yakuniy qiymatning joriy qiymati sifatida baholash.
dcf-valuation.body:
Diskontlangan pul oqimlari (DCF) asosida baholash biznes u yaratadigan erkin pul oqimlarining joriy qiymatiga teng ekanini aytadi. Bosqichlar: firmaning erkin pul oqimini (soliqdan keyingi operatsion foyda + amortizatsiya − CapEx − aylanma kapitalning oshishi) aniq davr uchun, odatda 5–10 yilga prognoz qilish; undan keyingi barcha pul oqimlari uchun yakuniy qiymatni baholash; hammasini WACC bo‘yicha diskontlash; so‘ng kapital qiymatini olish uchun sof qarzni ayirish.

Yakuniy qiymat odatda Gordon o‘sish formulasidan foydalanadi: TV = FCFₙ₊₁ ÷ (WACC − g), bu yerda g — uzoq muddatli o‘sish sur’ati bo‘lib, u WACC dan past bo‘lishi va iqtisodiyotning uzoq muddatli nominal o‘sishidan oshmasligi kerak.

Misol (million AQSh dollari): prognoz qilingan FCF 1–3-yillarda 100, 110 va 121, WACC 12%, uzoq muddatli o‘sish 4%. 3-yil oxiridagi TV = 121 × 1,04 ÷ (0,12 − 0,04) = 125,84 ÷ 0,08 ≈ 1 573. Joriy qiymatlar: 100 ÷ 1,12 = 89,3; 110 ÷ 1,2544 = 87,7; 121 ÷ 1,4049 = 86,1; yakuniy qiymat esa 1 573 ÷ 1,4049 ≈ 1 119,6. Korxona qiymati ≈ 89,3 + 87,7 + 86,1 + 1 119,6 ≈ 1 383. Sof qarz 300 bo‘lsa, kapital qiymati ≈ 1 083; 100 million aksiya bilan bir aksiya taxminan 10,8 turadi.

E’tibor bering, yakuniy qiymat jami qiymatning taxminan 81% ini tashkil etadi. WACC yoki g dagi kichik o‘zgarishlar javobni sezilarli o‘zgartiradi: g = 4% o‘rniga 5% bo‘lsa, TV taxminan 1 815 ga, korxona qiymati esa taxminan 1 555 ga ko‘tariladi. Har doim WACC va g bo‘yicha sezgirlik jadvalini taqdim eting va nazarda tutilgan o‘sish hamda marjalar real ekanini tekshiring.

Asosiy xulosa: DCF qiymati = prognoz qilingan erkin pul oqimlarining joriy qiymati + yakuniy qiymatning joriy qiymati, so‘ng kapital qiymati uchun sof qarz ayiriladi. Natija farazlar qanchalik yaxshi bo‘lsa, shunchalik yaxshi, shuning uchun ularning sezgirligini tekshiring.

valuation-multiples.title: Baholash multiplikatorlari va o‘xshash kompaniyalar
valuation-multiples.summary: EV/EBITDA va P/E yordamida kompaniyani o‘xshash bizneslar bilan solishtirib, tezda baholash.
valuation-multiples.body:
Nisbiy baholash kompaniyani o‘xshash kompaniyalar yoki yaqinda amalga oshirilgan bitimlar bilan solishtirib baholaydi. U to‘liq prognoz tuzish o‘rniga "investorlar shunga o‘xshash bizneslar uchun qancha to‘lamoqda?" degan savolga javob beradi va har qanday DCF uchun qimmatli o‘zaro tekshiruv hisoblanadi.

Avval ikkita qiymat o‘lchovini farqlang. Kapital qiymati (bozor kapitallashuvi) = aksiya narxi × muomaladagi aksiyalar soni. Korxona qiymati (EV) — butun biznesning barcha kapital beruvchilar uchun qiymati: EV = kapital qiymati + qarz − pul (kerak bo‘lganda ozchilik ulushlari va imtiyozli aksiyalar qo‘shiladi). Har birini mos ko‘rsatkich bilan juftlang: EV ni EBITDA, EBIT yoki tushum kabi foizlargacha bo‘lgan ko‘rsatkichlar bilan; kapital qiymatini esa sof foyda kabi foizlardan keyingi ko‘rsatkichlar bilan.

Keng tarqalgan multiplikatorlar: EV/EBITDA, EV/tushum (zarar ko‘rayotgan, tez o‘sayotgan firmalar uchun) va narxning foydaga nisbati, P/E = aksiya narxi ÷ bir aksiyaga foyda. Misol: o‘xshash kompaniyalar o‘rtacha (mediana) 8x EV/EBITDA bilan savdo qilinadi. Bizning kompaniyamizning EBITDA si 190 million, demak uning nazarda tutilgan EV si = 8 × 190 = 1 520 million. 160 million sof qarzni ayirsak, kapital qiymati 1 360 million bo‘ladi; 100 million aksiya bilan bir aksiya taxminan 13,6 turadi.

Multiplikatorlar o‘sish, risk va kapital rentabelligi haqidagi farazlarni o‘z ichiga oladi, shuning uchun tarmoq, hajm, o‘sish, marjalar va bozor bo‘yicha haqiqatan o‘xshash kompaniyalarni tanlang va farqlarni hisobga oling. Raqobatchilaridan ikki baravar tez o‘sayotgan kompaniya yuqoriroq multiplikatorga loyiq. EBITDA yoki foydani buzadigan bir martalik moddalarga e’tibor bering va boshqa mamlakat yoki qizib ketgan bozordagi multiplikatorlar to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri mos kelmasligi mumkinligini yodda tuting.

Asosiy xulosa: EV = kapital qiymati + sof qarz. EV multiplikatorlarini foizlargacha bo‘lgan ko‘rsatkichlar bilan, kapital multiplikatorlarini esa foizlardan keyingi ko‘rsatkichlar bilan ishlating, haqiqatan o‘xshash kompaniyalarni tanlang va DCF bilan solishtirib tekshiring.
